signals.title: Auxiliary title generation fails with HTTP 400 on DeepSeek: response_format json_schema unsupported
signals.text: ## Bug Description Every new session prints: ``` ⚠ Auxiliary title generation failed: HTTP 400: This response_format type is unavailable now ``` when the main model provider is DeepSeek (official API, `deepseek-chat`). Session auto-titling silently never happens. ## Root Cause `agent/title_generator.py` sends: ```python extra_body={"response_format": _TITLE_RESPONSE_FORMAT} ``` where `_TITLE_RESPONSE_FORMAT` is OpenAI's **structured-outputs** format: ```python _TITLE_RESPONSE_FORMAT = { "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "session_title", "strict": True, "schema": {...}}, } ``` The DeepSeek API does **not** support `response_format.type == "json_schema"` (it only supports `json_object`), so the request fails with HTTP 400 before the model ever responds. `_extract_title_text()` has robust fallbacks (loose JSON scan, prose fallback) precisely for providers that ignore `response_format`, but those fallbacks never get a chance to run because the request itself is rejected. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure main model as DeepSeek official API (`deepseek-chat`) 2. Start a new session in the CLI 3. Observe: `⚠ Auxiliary title generation failed: HTTP 400: This response_format type is unavailable now` ## Expected Behavior Title generation should work with providers that don't support `json_schema` response_format — either by provider-aware format selection (fall back to `json_object` or omit `response_format` for DeepSeek et al.) or by catching the 400 and retrying without `response_format` (the existing extraction fallbacks already handle non-structured responses). ## Workaround ```bash hermes config set auxiliary.title_generation.provider google ``` (Gemini supports the `json_schema` response format, so titling works when routed there.) ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.2 (2026.8.16) - Provider: DeepSeek official API (`deepseek-chat`) - WSL2 (Ubuntu), CLI
signals.author: fengxy1982

signals.title: Windows: `hermes update` self-locks its own console-script launcher; ZIP fallback masks it and leaves the venv editable install stale
signals.text: ## Summary On Windows, invoking `hermes update` via the console-script launcher (`venv\Scripts\hermes.exe`) guarantees the update's dependency step fails: the update process itself runs from the very executable `uv pip install -e .[all]` must replace. Windows blocks delete/replace of a running image (`os error 32`), the quarantine/rename also fails (PermissionError), and the updater silently falls back to the ZIP download — source tree updated, venv console scripts not. Result: every update leaves a stale editable install that must be repaired by hand with `uv pip install -e .`. ## Environment - Windows 11, official installer layout: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe` - Update invoked as `& "…\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe" update --backup` (scripted, e.g. PowerShell update script) - Hermes v0.20.x, `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` (post-`927463efc` extraction) ## Repro 1. Run `hermes update` via the launcher exe (the normal `hermes update` on PATH), with or without the Desktop app running. 2. Observe, on every full update run: ``` ⚠ Could not quarantine hermes.exe (PermissionError: another process is holding it open). ⚠ Git update failed: Command '[…\bin\uv.exe', 'pip', 'install', '-e', '.']' returned non-zero exit status 2. → Falling back to ZIP download... ✓ Updated N items from ZIP ⚠ Could not quarantine hermes.exe (PermissionError: another process is holding it open). (retry) ``` 3. Update exits 0. Tree is on new main, but `venv\Scripts\hermes.exe` is the old launcher and the editable install was never refreshed. `uv pip install -e .` is required manually — and it too fails while any `hermes.exe` process is alive. ## Evidence - 4 consecutive full update runs failed identically (2026-08-14 22:30, 08-15 22:36, 08-16 12:38, 08-17 21:25 — local). Desktop app **closed** for the 08-17 run: same failure. The only `hermes.exe` guaranteed present every run is the updater's own launcher process. - Two runs that "succeeded" (08-15 22:39, 08-16 12:41) found zero new commits, skipped the dependency step entirely, and only ran "Refreshed Windows gateway launcher scripts" — no pip step, no lock, no failure. Confirms the failure is specific to the dependency/venv-refresh phase. - `hermes update --help` (v0.20.3) documents the known hazard: `--force` "…will likely cause WinError 32 warnings and may leave a reboot-deferred .exe replacement"; `--force-venv` mutates the venv anyway. Neither avoids the failure for the launcher-invoked path. ## Root-cause analysis (code receipts, HEAD a3995f8ae) 1. The Windows shim guard only checks for **another** `hermes.exe` (`hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:4487-4497`, "abort early if another hermes.exe is holding the venv shim open… See issue #26670"). The calling instance is excluded, so a launcher-invoked update never self-triggers the abort. 2. `_detect_venv_python_processes` likewise excludes "the calling process and its ancestors" (`update_cmd.py:3193-3211`), and its docstring concedes the shim guard misses the venv-`python.exe` lock-holder class (Desktop `hermes serve` backend keeping `.pyd`s mapped). The complementary blind spot is the **self-shim**: the launcher process (`hermes.exe`) holds its own image mapped for the whole update. 3. The dependency step runs `uv pip install -e .[all]` (`update_cmd.py:2025`) — which removes and recreates `venv\Scripts\hermes.exe`. With the shim alive, the remove fails (`os error 32`) and the quarantine rename (`hermes_cli/main.py:8928`, "Could not quarantine…") also fails on this Windows build. 4. On failure the updater prints "→ Falling back to ZIP download..." (`update_cmd.py:6562`), extracts the source tree, and continues to exit 0 — **without refreshing the venv**, and without a final warning that the editable install is stale. ## Why --force / --force-venv don't fix this path - `--force` bypasses the shim guard but the `uv` child still hits the locked file → same exit 2 → same ZIP fallback. - `--force-venv` mutates the venv but leaves the launcher replacement reboot-deferred. - The real fix is that the update must not run as the file it replaces. ## Suggested fixes (ranked) 1. **Run the venv-refresh phase from `python.exe`, not the shim.** The updater could respawn its dependency step as `venv\Scripts\python.exe -m …` (detached), or simply document/recommend on Windows: `venv\Scripts\python.exe -m hermes_cli.main update`. Verified working invocation: the Desktop backend and gateway already run as `python.exe -m hermes_cli.main …`; a python-based updater never locks the shim. 2. **Defer shim replacement to process exit:** quarantine via rename *after* the launcher exits, or write the new shim to a temp name and swap on next boot/start. 3. **At minimum, detect the self-shim case pre-flight** (launcher-invoked, Windows) and either refuse with the correct remediation ("re-run via `python -m hermes_cli.main update`") or warn loudly before the pip step. 4. **ZIP fallback must not look successful:** when the venv refresh was skipped, print a final, explicit line (e.g. "venv not refreshed — run `uv pip install -e .` or `python -m hermes_cli.main update` to complete") and/or set a nonzero/flag status instead of exiting 0. ## Impact Every launcher-invoked update on Windows leaves the editable install stale while reporting success. Users must discover the manual reinstall themselves; the venv can also be left half-synced (the exact corruption class `baecc840e` and the 8/14-8/15 `19cff8930`/`92c998c86` fixes guard against). Low blast radius but high annoyance on the primary supported desktop OS. ## Related - Issue #26670 (shim guard design) - `19cff8930` fix(update): complete pending core install before any native import (self-lock loop fix) - `92c998c86` fix(update): restore quarantined hermes.exe shims after no-op installs on Windows - `535b46f81` feat: ZIP-based update fallback for Windows

signals.title: operational surfaces have no structured output — gateway status, cron list, dispatch-status are human-text only, and the only alternative source (gateway.log) contains message content
signals.text: ## The gap Board-query commands ship `--json` (`kanban boards list`, `stats`, `diagnostics`, `activity`, `sessions activity`) — but every *operational* surface is human-formatted text only. Measured on 2026-08-17, all of these reject `--json`: ``` hermes gateway status hermes cron list hermes kanban runs hermes kanban dispatch-status hermes pause status hermes curator status ``` ## Why it matters An external observer (dashboard, alerting sweep, healthcheck) that wants to answer three basic operator questions — *is the gateway's channel alive, did the last cron delivery succeed, was a command refused* — has exactly one machine-readable source left: `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log`. That file is unusable as a privacy-safe source by construction: - inbound messages are logged with full user text (`inbound message: ... msg='...'`) — measured, 39 of 2,944 lines in a live install - even the single `Unauthorized user:` line carries the platform user id and display name - the log format is not a contract; adjacent lines can change shape on any release So a downstream tool must either parse a log that contains private conversation content, or answer "Unknown". We chose Unknown, but the questions are real: in one live install a refused-command path stayed silently closed for five days because the only record was one WARNING line in that log. `hermes monitoring` describes itself as *"content-free by construction — no prompts, messages, tool args/results"*, which is exactly the right posture — but it currently only exports over OTLP when configured, and `monitoring status` has no structured output either. ## Suggestion A content-free structured status read, wherever it fits best — e.g. `hermes monitoring status --json` or `hermes gateway status --json` — carrying counts/states/timestamps only: - platform connections: state + last successful outbound delivery timestamp per platform - cron: per-job `last_status` / `last_run_at` / `next_run_at` (this already exists in `cron/jobs.json`, but that file is an internal, not a contract) - command refusals: a counter since start, no identities - dispatcher: last tick timestamp, spawned/reaped counters The same "counts and states only" discipline the kanban `--json` surfaces already follow would make the whole operational layer observable without any consumer ever needing to open the logs.

signals.title: [Bug] Desktop profile rail shows every profile twice with a 'macmini' host chip after v0.20.3 upgrade
signals.text: ## Bug: Desktop profile rail lists every profile twice with a "macmini" host chip after upgrading to v0.20.3 (Bot Mode) After updating the desktop client to **v0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2)**, the profile rail (sidebar / profile switcher) renders every pre-existing profile **twice**: - one row with no chip (the original profile) - one duplicated row with a small grey chip that reads `macmini` (the short hostname of the machine the Hermes gateway is running on) The local `hermes profile list` (CLI) does **not** show duplicates — only the new desktop client does. The `macmini` chip is the new connection's host label being appended to the profile name where it should be filtered out. ### Repro 1. Run any Hermes install with the desktop client on Mac (or any host). Have a Hermes gateway running on a machine named `macmini` (the host short name). 2. Pre-existing profiles: e.g. `default`, `admin`, `operator`, `ta-ra`, `secops-guard`, `sysadmin-core`, `iifr-ecp-marketing`, `coder`, `analyst`, `verifier`, `planner`, `research`, `creative`, `creative-studio`, `devops`, `architect`, `bot`, `ads-manager`, `bd`, `council`, `moa`, `latticed-bd`, `latticed-creative`, `latticed-campaign`, `cosmicmandalas`, `iifr-ecp-marketing`, `teaching`. 3. Each profile is also reachable via the locally running gateway on the macmini host. 4. Open the desktop profile switcher / Bot Mode roster. ### Expected Each profile appears exactly once. The host chip is only shown when the profile is **remote** (different host than the local connection), not when the profile is reachable on the local gateway. ### Actual The roster shows **every** profile twice, once with no chip and once with the `macmini` chip. The duplicate rows are all `stopped` from the gateway's perspective — they exist only because the desktop roster is enumerating both the local profile list and the gateway-reported profile list as one row each, keyed by name alone, and then the gateway rows are tagged with `host.label`. ### Likely cause Two suggestion sources for the roster that are not being deduplicated on the `(host, profile)` tuple: - `RosterKey` / `host.request('profiles.list', {})` — the local profile set (one row per profile, no host chip) - `host.requestProfile(...)` / `profiles.list` from the **remote** gateway connection — the same profiles again, each tagged with the remote connection's host label (`macmini`) The merge key is `profile.name` only, so the two rows are kept side-by-side as an apparent duplicate. The same dup pattern is used in `connections-registry.tsx` for SSH dupes (keyed on `user@host:port + remoteProfile`), but the Bot Mode roster merge is not applying the same dedupe. ### Observed (screenshot) [Murali Mac Mini, 2026-08-18] Profile rail scrolled to the second page. Every row in the viewport shows a grey `macmini` chip. The pre-existing (no-chip) versions of the same profiles are visible above the viewport when scrolled to the top — one row per profile, then a duplicate row with the host chip. ### Suggested fix In the Bot Mode / Hermes-Bots profile roster merge, dedupe on `(host, profile)` (the same key used in `connections-registry.tsx` for SSH connections) instead of on `profile.name` alone. When the same profile is reachable from the local connection and from a remote gateway whose host resolves to the same machine, surface only one row — the local one — and skip the remote copy. ### Workaround (local) Hide the `macmini`-tagged duplicates by right-clicking the header and using the eye toggle added in commit `133381508f` (Bot Mode: hide bots from the roster via right-click — header eye toggle reveals and unhides them) — but note this only hides the *remote* copy and leaves the local copy visible, which is the opposite of what you'd want for a true duplicate. ### Environment - Hermes Agent: **v0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2)** - macOS Mac Mini (host short name: `macmini`) - Desktop client connected to local gateway + gateway running on the same host - 27 profiles in `~/.hermes/profiles/` - 1 phantom profile (see related issue) ### Commits in v0.20.3 likely in the surrounding area - `133381508f feat(bot-mode): hide bots from the roster via right-click — header eye toggle reveals and unhides them` - `d89434e352 fix(desktop): Bots pane is a Sessions-zone tab again (not stacked below) and the Cronjobs pane only appears in Bots mode` - `4014eb7d5c fix(bot-mode): sweep CLI-born Bot Mode sessions out of the global sidebar (ownership-based)` - `e3db72d328 fix(desktop): fail-stop deleted-profile reconnects and evict the stale rail badge` - `b2c8a148e8 fix(desktop): fail-stop deleted-profile reconnects and evict the stale rail badge` Filed by: Mac Mini admin (Muralikrishnan) — `~/.hermes/profiles/admin/`

signals.title: [Bug] Profile directory '~/.hermes/profiles/0' is created without a config.yaml on v0.20.3 first launch
signals.text: ## Bug: Profile directory `~/.hermes/profiles/0` is created without a config.yaml on v0.20.3 first launch After updating to **v0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2)**, a profile directory named `0` (the literal digit zero) is created on first launch of the desktop client. It has no `config.yaml`, no `pairing/`, no `assets/avatar.png`, no `memories/`, but it does have a `state.db`, `projects.db`, `SOUL.md`, `cron/executions.db`, and a default Hermes `state.db` schema. The directory name `0` is a sentinel / placeholder that's not a valid profile name (existing profiles are like `admin`, `default`, `ta-ra`, `coder`, etc.). It looks like a profile bootstrap path that wasn't routed through the named profile validator. ### Repro 1. Update Hermes to v0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2). 2. Launch the desktop client for the first time after the update. 3. Open `~/.hermes/profiles/` and a `0` directory is present alongside the other profiles. ```bash $ ls -la ~/.hermes/profiles/ | grep -E 'macmini|0$' drwx------ 20 lyraai staff 640 Aug 18 06:53 0 ``` ```bash $ hermes profile list | grep ' 0 ' 0 — stopped — — ``` ### Expected Either no extra profile is created, or it's created with a real name and a valid `config.yaml` (e.g. `~/.hermes/profiles/default/config.yaml`). ### Actual `~/.hermes/profiles/0/` exists with the following contents: `.update_check`, `SOUL.md`, `assets/`, `audio_cache/`, `cache/schema_columns.json`, `cron/` (with `executions.db`, `.tick.lock`, `.jobs.lock`, `ticker_heartbeat`, `ticker_last_success`), `hooks/`, `image_cache/`, `logs/` (with `agent.log`, `gui.log`, `errors.log`), `memories/`, `pairing/`, `pets/`, `projects.db`, `sessions/`, `skills/` (with `.bundled_manifest` and a full skill bundle), `state.db`, `state.db-shm`, `state.db-wal`. **No `config.yaml`**. ```bash $ cat ~/.hermes/profiles/0/.update_check {"ts": 1787016066.552982, "behind": 0, "rev": null, "ver": "0.20.3"} $ cat ~/.hermes/profiles/0/SOUL.md You are Hermes Agent, an intelligent AI assistant created by Nous Research. You are helpful, knowledgeable, and direct. ... $ hermes profile describe 0 (no description set for '0') ``` ### Likely cause A profile-init codepath receives `0` (or a falsy value, or `null`, or an integer index) somewhere in the desktop client's roster bootstrap, and falls back to coercing the path component to a string. The directory is created with the bundled manifest but the `config.yaml` writer is name-aware and skips creating the file when the name is not a valid slug. The net effect is a half-initialized profile that the CLI lists, the desktop roster shows as a profile named `0`, and the gateway ignores. ### Suggested fix - Validate the profile name against the slug pattern (`/^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$/`) before creating a profile directory. Reject and skip when the name is empty, `0`, or a number. - Or: in the desktop roster merge, filter out profiles whose path component is the literal digit `0` or otherwise not a valid slug. ### Workaround (local) ```bash # After stopping the gateway: rm -rf ~/.hermes/profiles/0 # (verify before deleting — see ~/.hermes/profiles/_backups/ and ~/.hermes/profiles/_archived/ for malformed profiles already moved aside) ``` ### Environment - Hermes Agent: **v0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2)** - Installed: 2026-08-18 06:51 (the `0` directory's `.update_check` confirms it was created alongside the v0.20.3 install) - macOS Mac Mini - 27 valid profiles in `~/.hermes/profiles/` (`default`, `admin`, `operator`, `ta-ra`, `secops-guard`, `sysadmin-core`, `iifr-ecp-marketing`, `coder`, `analyst`, `verifier`, `planner`, `research`, `creative`, `creative-studio`, `devops`, `architect`, `bot`, `ads-manager`, `bd`, `council`, `moa`, `latticed-bd`, `latticed-creative`, `latticed-campaign`, `cosmicmandalas`, `teaching`, plus 4 symlinked sharing pets) + 1 phantom (`0`) ### Related observation The same v0.20.3 release also causes the profile rail to display every profile twice with a `macmini` host chip (see related issue). The phantom `0` profile appears alongside the duplicated rows in the same roster. Filed by: Mac Mini admin (Muralikrishnan) — `~/.hermes/profiles/admin/`

signals.title: feat(desktop): system-wide selection assistant — floating AI panel appears when selecting text in any app
signals.text: ## Summary Add a **system-wide selection assistant** like Cherry Studio's *Selection Assistant* (划词助手) and Doubao's *划词快捷助手*: whenever I select text in **any application** — browser, PDF reader, Word, code editor, terminal, anything — a small floating panel automatically appears right next to the selection, offering one-tap AI actions on that text. ## Desired experience 1. I select some text anywhere on the system. 2. A floating panel appears beside the selection (Cherry Studio / Doubao style), showing quick actions such as: - **Translate** - **Explain** - **Summarize** - **Ask Hermes…** (free-form question about the selection) 3. Clicking an action shows the answer **right there in the panel**, streamed live — no window switching, no copy-paste. 4. From the result I can: - **Copy** the answer - **Continue in Hermes** — jump into a full session carrying the selected text and the answer as context, so I can keep going with Hermes' full capabilities (tools, skills, memory) - Dismiss with Esc or by clicking away 5. The interaction should work regardless of which app has focus; the panel should feel lightweight and instant, like Cherry Studio's. Configurable: enable/disable, which actions appear, default action, target session for "continue" (new vs. current), custom prompt templates per action. ## Motivation Today, asking Hermes about something I'm reading is a 4-step context switch: select → copy → switch to Hermes → paste → type the question. That friction means I simply don't do it for quick things like translating a sentence or understanding a paragraph. With a selection assistant the loop becomes: **select → get the answer where I am**. For translation-heavy or reading-heavy workflows (documentation, papers, foreign-language content) this is the difference between reaching for Hermes constantly and not at all. Cherry Studio and Doubao have proven this is one of the most-used daily features for Chinese users especially; Hermes has the stronger agent behind it (tools, skills, memory, any provider) but no way to surface it at the point of reading. ## Precedents - **Cherry Studio** — Selection Assistant (划词助手): select text → floating panel with translate/explain/summarize/custom actions - **Doubao (豆包)** — 划词快捷助手, same pattern, system-wide - **PopClip** (macOS) + AI extensions — the same interaction family - In-repo, the in-chat half of this interaction is already requested: #66121 (floating "Reply with selection" button), #52554, #73138 — this issue is the system-wide half.

signals.title: [Bug]: macOS: hermes update reports success while the launchd reload helper dies before bootstrapping — gateway left unregistered for 36 min (post-#80491)
signals.text: ## Summary On macOS, `hermes update` printed `✓ Update complete! (v0.20.3)` and exited 0 while the `ai.hermes.gateway` LaunchAgent was left **unloaded from launchd** for 36 minutes. No warning was printed and no failure was logged. This is **not** #74973 (job already booted out *before* the update) and **not** the mechanism fixed by #80491 — that fix is present in my tree and its `FAILED` line never fired, because the helper died before reaching the code that writes it. Two independent gaps combine here: 1. The reload helper spawned by `launchd_reload()` can die **before its first bootstrap attempt**, leaving `launchd-reload.log` with only the "helper started" marker — no retry lines, no `FAILED` line (the post-#80491 failure line never runs). 2. `update_cmd.py` treats "`launchd_restart()` returned without raising" as success and appends the label to `restarted_services` with **no verification that a supervised PID exists**. Since the reload is asynchronous, any helper failure is invisible. ## Environment - Hermes Agent **v0.20.3**, git install, `main` @ `a3995f8` - Contains #80491 (`fe3a1cad6`, merged 2026-08-06) — verified via `git merge-base --is-ancestor` - macOS **26.6.1** (build 25G76), Apple Silicon (arm64) - Python 3.11.15 (venv) - Gateway installed as LaunchAgent `ai.hermes.gateway` (`KeepAlive=true`, `RunAtLoad=true`) ## Timeline (from my logs; paths redacted) ``` 08:56:04 launchd-reload.log: "Launchd reload helper started for gui/<uid>/ai.hermes.gateway" --> and then NOTHING, ever. No attempt lines. No FAILED line. 08:56:06 gateway.log: Received SIGTERM Shutdown context: signal=SIGTERM under_systemd=yes parent_pid=1 --> PPID=1 means the job WAS loaded and launchd-supervised at this moment 08:56:12 Exiting with code 1 (signal-initiated shutdown without restart request) 08:56:14 gateway-exit-diag.log: gateway.start pid=36740 argv: [".../hermes_cli/main.py", "gateway", "run", "--replace", "--external-supervisor"] 08:56:18 Received SIGTERM as a planned gateway stop -- exiting cleanly Shutdown context: signal=SIGTERM under_systemd=no parent_pid=36734 --> killed by the update process, NOT by launchd 08:56:22 gateway.exit_clean pid=36740 --> no further gateway.start in gateway-exit-diag.log 09:13 update prints "✓ Update complete! (v0.20.3)", exit 0 <-- gateway is DOWN 09:32 I manually ran: launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <plist> <-- recovered ``` `launchctl print gui/<uid>/ai.hermes.gateway` during the window: `Could not find service "ai.hermes.gateway" in domain for user gui: <uid>` The plist file itself was intact the whole time (mtime 08:56, rewritten by the update). ## Why this is distinct from #80491 #80491 is in my tree and its logic is present in `hermes_cli/gateway.py` — the helper script requires a positive PID rather than a bare exit-0, and writes a `FAILED launchd reload for ... service NOT registered` line to `launchd-reload.log` when the retry budget is exhausted. That `FAILED` line **never appeared**. The helper never got far enough to run it. The generated `reload_script` opens with `sleep 2`, and the update's parent process exited during that window — so the whole helper went away before its first `launchctl bootout` / `bootstrap`. So #80491 correctly hardened *how success is judged once the helper runs*; it does not cover *the helper not surviving to run at all*. ## Why this is distinct from #74973 / #75021 #74973's repro step 3 requires `launchctl list | grep ai.hermes.gateway` to be **empty** before the update starts. In my case the opposite held: at 08:56:06 the gateway logged `under_systemd=yes parent_pid=1`, i.e. it was alive and launchd-supervised. #75021's reworked helper still ends with: ```python launchd_restart() return [label] # success is assumed, never verified ``` Only `subprocess.CalledProcessError` triggers `_warn_launchd_gateway_left_down()`. My failure raises nothing: `launchd_restart()` takes the `_request_gateway_self_restart(pid)` branch and returns normally, the async helper dies silently afterwards. So #75021 as written would still report success here. ## Empirically ruled out I probed these on the affected machine before filing, to save reviewer time: 1. **`launchctl submit` is NOT dead on macOS 26.6.1.** A probe job submitted via `launchctl submit -l <label> -o <log> -- /bin/bash -c 'echo PROBE_OK'` ran and wrote its output. The mechanism itself works. 2. **`launchctl bootout` does NOT kill the `launchctl submit` script that issued it.** A 4-step probe (echo -> bootout -> echo -> sleep 2 -> echo -> bootstrap -> echo) completed all four steps. Self-termination is not the cause. ## Additional finding: `bootstrap` can return rc=0 without registering While probing I hit a state worth flagging independently: ``` bootout_rc=0 bootstrap_rc=0 --> launchctl list <label>: not registered ``` A standalone retry moments later registered fine. So on macOS 26.6.1 a `bootstrap` issued shortly after a `bootout` can report success while the service is not actually registered. This reinforces #80491's direction: **success must be judged by a live supervised PID, never by an exit code** — and that rule needs to apply to the `update_cmd.py` caller too, not just inside the helper. ## Impact Messaging adapters and all cron jobs stayed dark for 36 minutes. `KeepAlive` cannot help because the job definition was deregistered. The only signal was that the bot stopped replying — `hermes update` itself reported success. ## Suggested direction (not a patch) After `launchd_restart()` returns, poll for a supervised PID (`launchctl list <label>` reporting a positive PID) for a bounded window before appending to `restarted_services`. If it never appears, print the same `_warn_launchd_gateway_left_down()` warning that the `CalledProcessError` path already prints. That closes the async gap without depending on the helper's own liveness. Note: an equivalent post-restart verification gap was reported and fixed on the systemd side (#6631) but was never applied to the macOS path. ## Workaround for other users ```bash # after any `hermes update` on macOS: launchctl list | grep ai.hermes.gateway || \ launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway.plist ```

signals.title: [Bug]: TUI session switch leaks queued /q message to the newly-active session
signals.text: ## Bug Description In the Hermes TUI (Ink), a queued message submitted via `/q` is routed to whichever session is **active at send time**, not the session that was active when the input was submitted. Switching sessions between submit and send leaks the message to the wrong session. ## Repro 1. Open two TUI sessions: A (the one you intend to message) and B (another). 2. In session A, type `/q what took you so long` (intended as a one-shot query to A; in this case the user was looking for a `/prompt`-style editor command). 3. **Before** the `/q` is processed, switch to session B (e.g. via the session list / keybind). 4. The `/q what took you so long` message lands in session B, and B's agent answers it as if the user had sent it there. ## Expected The `/q` payload is bound to the session that was active at input-submit time. Session switching after submit must not re-target the message. ## Actual The active-session pointer is read at send time, so a mid-flight session switch re-targets the queued message to the newly-active session. The agent in B responds to a message the user never sent to it. ## Environment - Surface: TUI (Ink) — NOT desktop. All existing session-switch-leak reports (#46194, #46732, #62823, #86106) are tagged `comp/desktop`; this is the TUI variant. - Platform: Windows 11, MSYS/git-bash - Reproducible: yes (happened once during normal use; switching between two live TUI sessions) ## Likely area The session-send path reads `active_session` at dispatch rather than capturing it when the `/q` input is submitted. Symptom mirrors #46194 but on the TUI surface — likely a shared session-routing helper, not desktop-specific UI code. ## Notes - Related: #46194 (desktop variant of the same symptom), #46732, #62823, #86106 — all `comp/desktop`. - Did not investigate the fix; user asked only to report.
signals.author: rizkyaditya-git

signals.title: feat(gateway): add Zulip integration and messaging support
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? This PR adds Zulip support to Hermes as a bundled platform plugin under `plugins/platforms/zulip/`. The original branch predated the current platform plugin system and wired Zulip through several core gateway, CLI, scheduler, and tool files. This update moves the integration onto the current plugin path: platform registration, setup metadata, env/YAML configuration, auth validation, adapter construction, cron delivery metadata, standalone text delivery, and the Zulip search tool now live with the plugin. The goal is to keep Zulip support aligned with the current platform architecture while preserving the adapter behavior that has been tested by real users. ## Related Issue Related to the earlier Zulip PRs: - #16541 - #54715 This PR remains the canonical Zulip candidate per maintainer feedback on this thread. Fixes # ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [x] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `plugins/platforms/zulip/` - Adds the Zulip platform plugin, adapter, plugin metadata, standalone sender, setup/config hooks, and Zulip search tool. - Supports DMs, stream topics, mention/free-response handling, thread/session isolation, topic names containing `/`, media handling, typing/reactions where supported, and edit-based streaming. - `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `tools/lazy_deps.py` - Adds Zulip as an optional/lazy dependency through the `zulip` extra. - `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/zulip.md` - Adds Zulip setup, configuration, cron delivery, standalone send, search, and streaming docs. - `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/index.md` - Lists Zulip in the messaging platform docs. - `tests/gateway/test_zulip.py` - Adds gateway/plugin adapter coverage. - `tests/tools/test_zulip_search_messages.py` - Adds coverage for Zulip message search behavior. - `tests/test_project_metadata.py` - Adds coverage for Zulip dependency/plugin metadata wiring. This revision also incorporates updates from @slav's patches and @a6patch's branch work, manually integrated into the plugin structure to keep this PR reviewable: - Current-Hermes compatibility updates. - Zulip connected-state checking. - Platform registry support with standalone sender behavior. - Reconnect compatibility coverage. - Zulip message edit capability. - `edit_message(..., finalize=..., metadata=...)` support for gateway streaming. - Docs/tests for edit-based Zulip streaming. - Cron and standalone delivery validation. ## How to Test 1. Install with the Zulip extra, or with all extras: ```bash UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=venv uv sync --locked --extra zulip ``` or: ```bash UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=venv uv sync --locked --extra all ``` 2. Configure Zulip credentials and run setup/gateway: ```bash hermes setup hermes gateway ``` 3. Validate normal gateway behavior from Zulip: - Send the bot a DM. - Mention the bot in a stream topic. - Test a topic containing `/`, such as `some/topics/with/slashes`. - Attach an image and confirm the agent can see it. - Use `zulip_search_messages` from a Zulip conversation. 4. Validate standalone send with a configured home channel: ```bash hermes send --to zulip "Standalone Zulip send smoke" ``` 5. Validate cron delivery: ```bash hermes cron create \ --name zulip-cron-smoke \ --deliver "zulip:5:Sauve Cloud Status" \ --repeat 1 \ --script zulip-cron-smoke.sh \ --no-agent \ "every 1d" \ "Zulip cron smoke" hermes cron run zulip-cron-smoke ``` 6. Validate edit-based streaming by enabling both the global/root streaming flag and the Zulip platform streaming flag: ```yaml display: streaming: true platforms: zulip: streaming: true ``` 7. Run focused tests: ```bash pytest tests/gateway/test_zulip.py tests/tools/test_zulip_search_messages.py tests/ test_project_metadata.py -q ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [ ] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/ CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate. Related Zulip PRs are #16541 and #54715; this PR is the canonical Zulip candidate per maintainer feedback. - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/ A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide] (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform- compatibility) — or N/A - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A ## Screenshots / Logs Manually validated: - Zulip gateway startup and connection. - Inbound DM handling. - Stream/topic handling. - Topics containing `/`. - Thread/session isolation. - Zulip message search. - Image reception and vision support. - Standalone send using the configured Zulip home channel. - Cron delivery to Zulip. - Edit-in-place streaming. Example standalone send result: ```text hermes send --to zulip "Standalone Zulip send smoke" Sent to zulip home channel (chat_id: 5:Sauve Cloud Status) ``` ## Notes / Follow-Ups Edit-based streaming requires the global/root gateway streaming setting to be enabled in addition to the Zulip platform setting. Users should also be aware that Zulip may retain message edit history depending on the organization's Zulip settings. Two shared follow-ups were found while testing this PR: 1. Direct CLI sends to a specific Zulip topic, such as `hermes send --to "zulip:stream:topic" ...`, need one small shared sender fix outside of the Zulip plugin. This will be proposed separately after the plugin PR lands. 2. One-shot cron jobs using `--repeat 1` can sometimes deliver correctly but still print a failure status after completion. This appears to overlap with #57689, so it is not included here.

signals.title: fix: add system prompt guidance when Tool Search is active
signals.text: ## Problem When Tool Search activates and defers MCP/plugin tools behind the bridge tools (`tool_search`/`tool_describe`/`tool_call`), there is no system prompt guidance telling the model to search for deferred tools before concluding a capability is unavailable. **Observed behavior:** User asks "what is my first meeting tomorrow?" The model sees a `google-workspace` skill in the skills listing, loads it, finds missing OAuth credentials, and tells the user the capability isn't set up -- never discovering the fully-connected `mcp_google_workspace_get_events` tool that's deferred behind `tool_search`. **Expected behavior:** The model should call `tool_search("calendar")` before falling back to skills or giving up, discovering the connected MCP tool. ## Fix Add `TOOL_SEARCH_GUIDANCE` to `prompt_builder.py` and inject it into the system prompt when `tool_search` is in the session's `valid_tool_names`. Follows the existing pattern used by `MEMORY_GUIDANCE`, `SESSION_SEARCH_GUIDANCE`, and `SKILLS_GUIDANCE`. The guidance tells the model: - MCP and plugin tools are loaded on demand via `tool_search` - Always call `tool_search` before concluding a capability is unavailable - Deferred MCP tools are fully connected and authenticated - Prefer them over skill-based alternatives that may require separate setup 12 lines across 2 files, no new dependencies. Signed-off-by: Chris van Hoof <vanhoof@ouwish.com>

signals.title: feat(skills): add optional Pencil (pencil.dev) design skill
signals.text: ## Summary Adds an **optional** `creative/pencil` skill under `optional-skills/` — **not active by default**. Install explicitly: ```bash hermes skills install official/creative/pencil ``` Then Hermes can drive [Pencil](https://pencil.dev) (`.pen` design files in-repo) through the `pencil` CLI via the `terminal` tool. - **Zero core footprint, lazy deps.** Nothing in Hermes core; `pencil` is user-installed (`npm install -g @pencil.dev/cli`) only when using the skill. - **Three modes, in order of preference:** - **A — headless MCP via `pencil start`** (emerging): a headless session Hermes talks to over MCP with Pencil's real tools, wired through `hermes mcp add` — no REPL wrapper. Gated on the CLI actually exposing `start`. - **B — REPL wrapper** (`pencil interactive` piped via `scripts/pencil_repl.py`): the current fallback. - **C — prompt-driven** `pencil --out … --prompt …` (Pencil's embedded agent; needs an agent API key). ## Incorporated Pencil-team feedback (PR review) 1. **Learn the CLI at runtime, don't hardcode.** Pencil's commands/tools/`batch_design` schema change between releases. The skill now leads with runtime discovery — `pencil --help`, `pencil interactive --help` (prints the live tool reference), and `get_editor_state({ include_schema: true })` — and `references/mcp-tools.md` is explicitly a drift-prone primer that defers to those sources. `pencil_doctor.py` reads `pencil --help` and reports which integration path the installed build exposes. 2. **Prefer the headless `pencil start` + MCP path** for agents without a REPL loop. Documented as Mode A and detected by the doctor, but **gated**: the currently published `@pencil.dev/cli` ships no `start` command yet, so the skill tells the agent to confirm via `pencil --help` / `pencil start --help` before wiring (avoiding a dead command). Flips to Mode A automatically once the build supports it. ## Verified, not guessed Re-checked the live published CLI: it still only exposes `login/status/version/interactive` + agent mode (plus new `--workspace`/`--repo`), so `start` is genuinely emerging. Auth remains mandatory even headless; `batch_design` binding names are per-call; Node 22+ may be required (`ERR_REQUIRE_ESM`). ## Files - `optional-skills/creative/pencil/SKILL.md` - `optional-skills/creative/pencil/scripts/{pencil_repl,pencil_doctor}.py` - `optional-skills/creative/pencil/references/mcp-tools.md` - `tests/skills/test_pencil_skill.py` ## Test plan - [x] `pytest tests/skills/test_pencil_skill.py` — 20 passed (incl. runtime-discovery contract + `pencil --help` capability detection) - [x] `pytest tests/website/test_generate_skill_docs.py tests/test_plugin_skills.py` — 35 passed - [x] Doctor smoke-tested; no lint errors - [x] Rebased onto latest `main`

signals.title: fix(ssh): preflight sync-back size before tar download
signals.text: ## Summary - add a remote `.hermes` size preflight before SSH sync-back starts streaming a tarball into local `/tmp` - prefer GNU `du -sb`, with BSD/macOS `du -sk` fallback converted to bytes - refuse oversized sync-back before download using the existing `_SYNC_BACK_MAX_BYTES` cap - add focused unit tests for oversize refusal, invalid size output, preflight failure, successful tar streaming, and BSD fallback command shape ## Why In a production SSH-backed worker setup, remote `/root/.hermes` grew to several GiB. During worker cleanup Hermes streamed `tar cf - -C / root/.hermes` into local `/tmp/tmp*.tar`; the existing 2 GiB cap only runs after the tar is downloaded, so the Hermes host disk filled before sync-back could be rejected. Failing before the tar stream protects the host from disk pressure while preserving the existing post-download cap as a second line of defence. ## Test Plan ```bash python3 -m py_compile tools/environments/ssh.py tests/tools/test_ssh_bulk_upload.py python3 -m pytest tests/tools/test_ssh_bulk_upload.py -q -o 'addopts=' python3 -m pytest tests/tools/test_file_sync_back.py tests/tools/test_ssh_environment.py tests/tools/test_ssh_bulk_upload.py -q -o 'addopts=' git diff --check ``` Results locally: ```text 26 passed in 0.70s 58 passed, 11 skipped in 1.32s ```

signals.title: fix(compression): add hard message-count safety valve to TUI/CLI preflight path
signals.text: ## Summary The gateway has had a hard message-count safety valve since #4750 (`gateway/run.py`), but the TUI/CLI preflight path (`agent/turn_context.py`) lacks an equivalent backstop. When `should_defer_preflight_to_real_usage()` (#50762) keeps deferring compression because the last successful API call's `prompt_tokens` were below threshold, a TUI session can grow unbounded until the provider starts disconnecting — at which point no usage data is returned to update the compressor, creating an **unrecoverable death spiral**. ### The death spiral 1. Session grows past the compression threshold 2. `should_defer_preflight_to_real_usage()` defers compression (last successful API call was below threshold, growth within 5% tolerance) 3. Session continues growing — API still succeeds (model context > threshold) 4. `last_real_prompt_tokens` exceeds threshold → `should_defer` returns `False` 5. `should_compress()` should fire, but **anti-thrashing** (`_ineffective_compression_count >= 2`) can block it if prior compressions were ineffective 6. Provider starts timing out / disconnecting → no usage data returned 7. No usage → `last_prompt_tokens` stays stale → compression never triggers 8. Every subsequent message repeats the cycle → session is unrecoverable ### What this PR does | Layer | Change | |---|---| | `ContextCompressor.__init__` | New `hygiene_hard_message_limit` param (default 0 = disabled) | | `agent_init.py` | Reads `compression.hygiene_hard_message_limit` from config, passes to constructor | | `turn_context.py` preflight | When message count ≥ hard limit, bypasses deferral, cooldown, and anti-thrashing | | `should_compress()` | New `force` param — bypasses anti-thrashing when hard limit triggered | ### How it works The existing `compression.hygiene_hard_message_limit` config key (default 5000 in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`) was already used by the gateway hygiene layer. This PR extends it to the TUI/CLI preflight path — no new config key needed. When the message count exceeds the hard limit: - `should_defer_preflight_to_real_usage()` is bypassed (no more deferring) - `get_active_compression_failure_cooldown()` is bypassed (no cooldown blocking) - `should_compress(force=True)` bypasses anti-thrashing (no more ineffective-compression blocking) - Compression fires immediately ### Relationship to prior work - **#2153 / #4750**: Added the hard message-count safety valve to `gateway/run.py` (Layer 3). This PR extends the same concept to the TUI/CLI path. - **#36718 / #50762**: Added `should_defer_preflight_to_real_usage()` to prevent double-compression after a fresh compress. This PR adds an escape hatch when the session has grown too large. - **#27405**: Added the char-based preflight gate for few-huge-message sessions. This PR is orthogonal — it adds a count-based gate that fires regardless of token estimates. ## Files changed - `agent/context_compressor.py` — +15/-2 (`hygiene_hard_message_limit` field + `force` param) - `agent/turn_context.py` — +38/-11 (hard-limit check in preflight) - `agent/agent_init.py` — +9/-0 (config wiring) - `tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py` — +45/-0 (5 new tests) ## Test plan | | Result | |---|---| | `TestShouldCompress` (+2 force tests) | 6 passed | | `TestHygieneHardMessageLimit` (+3 new) | 3 passed | | `TestPreflightDeferral` (existing) | 5 passed | | `TestUpdateFromResponse` (existing) | 2 passed | | `py_compile` all 3 source files | OK | | Full file `test_context_compressor.py` | 130 passed | No existing tests modified — all additions are new test methods and a new test class.

signals.title: fix(tui_gateway): close slash_worker on WS detach to prevent memory leak
signals.text: ## Summary The Desktop app uses **one WebSocket for all sessions**. When the user switches sessions or the WS reconnects (e.g. after macOS sleep), old sessions are detached to `_detached_ws_transport` but their `slash_worker` subprocesses (**~13 MB each**) stay alive until the 6 h TTL reaper or 20 s orphan reaper fires — which may never happen if a background curator review keeps the session flagged as `running`. Over a few hours this accumulates dozens of idle workers, contributing to **GIL pressure** and **memory bloat**. In production this was observed as 17 zombie slash_workers (~230 MB) causing event-loop stalls up to 10.6 s. ## Changes ### 1. Close slash_worker on WS detach (core fix) `tui_gateway/server.py` — `_close_sessions_for_transport()`: When a session is detached (WS disconnect without `close_on_disconnect`), its `slash_worker` is now closed immediately instead of lingering. The worker is recreated lazily on the next slash command — both the `slash.exec` handler and `_restart_slash_worker` already handle `worker=None`. ### 2. Add INFO logging to `_close_session_by_id` (observability) Previously the entire session-close path was **completely silent** — no log at any level. This made it impossible to diagnose why sessions were or weren't being reaped. A single INFO line makes the teardown path visible: ``` INFO tui_gateway.server: session closed sid=abc123 end_reason=ws_orphan_reap ``` ## Why this is safe - `_SlashWorker.close()` is already idempotent (`_closed` guard + `poll()` guard) - `_finalize_session` (the session-end chokepoint, PR #42149) already closes the worker — our fix just closes it **sooner**, at detach time - The `slash.exec` handler creates a new worker on demand when `session["slash_worker"]` is `None` (server.py ~L12553) - `_restart_slash_worker` does the same after each turn ## Testing ``` tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_detach.py::test_close_sessions_for_transport_closes_worker_on_detach PASSED tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_detach.py::test_close_sessions_for_transport_preserves_worker_on_reap PASSED tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_detach.py::test_close_sessions_for_transport_handles_worker_close_exception PASSED tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_detach.py::test_close_session_by_id_logs_end_reason PASSED ``` All 24 existing slash_worker / ws_orphan / close_session tests still pass. ## Related work (complementary, non-overlapping) This PR addresses a **different leak path** from three open PRs. They are complementary and can all merge independently: | PR | Author | Fixes | Leak path | |---|---|---|---| | **#53308** | @pasevin | Drain thread join on close | 2 leaked threads per session | | **#41473** | @Fewmanism | Worker registry + idempotent close | Same-session-key duplicate workers | | **#48656** | @Nigmat-future | Startup orphan reaper + zombie parent detection | Workers surviving gateway crash | | **this PR** | — | Close worker on WS detach | Workers surviving session switch | ### Related issues - #48643 — slash_worker not reaped when session interrupted mid-compaction - #38095 — TUI slash worker zombie subprocesses leak after session close (CLOSED, #42149 merged) - #53303 — `_SlashWorker.close()` does not join drain threads - #48564 — RFC: Dashboard/TUI reliability hardening (umbrella)

signals.title: fix: keep shell fences rendered as code blocks
signals.text: ## Context Hermes Desktop can demote fenced snippets into prose when they look text-like. That breaks two related cases: - explicit `text`, `plain`, or `plaintext` fences can leak the language tag into rendered prose and lose the copyable code-card treatment (#57540 / #49972) - shell fence aliases can be misclassified as prose, letting literals like `$HOME` / `$USER` hit Markdown or math rendering ## Solution - Treat explicit `text`, `plain`, and `plaintext` fences as code by author intent in both preprocessing and render-time classification. - Keep common shell fence languages (`zsh`, `fish`, `powershell`, `cmd`, etc.) on the code path. - Continue demoting untagged / Markdown-tagged prose-looking fences. ## Verification - `npm exec vitest run src/lib/markdown-code.test.ts src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.test.ts -- --environment node` - `npx eslint src/lib/markdown-code.ts src/lib/markdown-code.test.ts src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.test.ts` - `npm run typecheck` - `git diff --check` ## Screenshots Before: ![Before: shell command fence rendered as prose](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DanSpicyTaco/hermes-agent/pr-assets-ui-output-formatting/before.png) After: ![After: shell command fence rendered as a code block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DanSpicyTaco/hermes-agent/pr-assets-ui-output-formatting/after.png)

signals.title: feat(compression): configurable max_tail_message_floor
signals.text: ## Summary PR #45259 hardened the compaction tail floor from a fixed 3 to `min(protect_last_n, 8)`. The cap of 8 was chosen to avoid preserving a whole run of bulky tool outputs on every compaction, but it is **not configurable** — users with large context windows and light tails (e.g. 340K context, `protect_last_n=20`) cannot raise it beyond 8, causing recent assistant replies to be summarized away even when plenty of context budget remains. This adds a `compression.max_tail_message_floor` config key (default `0` = use the module-level default of 8, preserving backward compatibility). Set it higher (e.g. `20`) to keep more recent messages verbatim during compaction at the cost of a smaller summarization window when tool outputs are bulky. ## Motivation On a 340K-context model with `protect_last_n: 12`, compression was firing frequently (token threshold 82% + message-count hard limit 400). The tail floor capped at 8 meant only the last 8 messages survived verbatim — detailed assistant replies from turns 9-12 back were folded into the LLM summary and lost detail. ## Changes | File | Change | |------|--------| | `agent/context_compressor.py` | Rename `_MAX_TAIL_MESSAGE_FLOOR` → `_DEFAULT_MAX_TAIL_MESSAGE_FLOOR`; add `max_tail_message_floor` ctor param + instance attr; add `_effective_max_tail_message_floor` property (returns config override or module default); use it in `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens` | | `agent/agent_init.py` | Read `compression.max_tail_message_floor` from config; pass to `ContextCompressor()` | | `hermes_cli/config.py` | Add `max_tail_message_floor: 0` to `DEFAULT_CONFIG["compression"]` | | `tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py` | `test_configurable_max_tail_message_floor` (floor=20 keeps ≥20 messages); `test_max_tail_message_floor_default_is_8` (backward compat) | ## Design - **Default `0` = backward compatible**: falls back to `_DEFAULT_MAX_TAIL_MESSAGE_FLOOR = 8`, identical to current behavior - **Token budget remains primary**: the 1.5x soft ceiling still wins; the floor only binds when the budget is exhausted - **`protect_last_n` still a minimum**: `min_tail_floor = max(3, min(protect_last_n, effective_floor))` — the floor caps `protect_last_n`, not the other way around ## Validation | Test | Result | |------|--------| | `test_configurable_max_tail_message_floor` | ✅ floor=20 keeps ≥20 tail messages | | `test_max_tail_message_floor_default_is_8` | ✅ default 0 → module default 8 | | Full compressor suite (153 tests) | ✅ 153 passed | | Windows footgun scan | ✅ No footguns found | | `py_compile` | ✅ OK | ## Config Example ```yaml compression: max_tail_message_floor: 20 # 0 = default 8; raise to keep more recent messages ``` ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) ## Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) - [x] My PR contains only changes related to this feature - [x] I have added tests for my changes - [x] I have tested on macOS (darwin-arm64) - [x] I have considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS)

signals.title: fix(config): auto-migrate stale profile config on serve/dashboard startup
signals.text: ## Problem After `hermes update` pulls new code (which bumps `_config_version` in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`), only the **active** (default) profile's config is migrated. Named profiles (e.g. `orchestrator`) keep their stale config version, so when the desktop app spawns `hermes serve --profile <name>` against the updated code, agent init fails with: ``` No LLM provider configured. Run `hermes model` to select a provider ``` The user sees prompts being silently rejected with no indication that the config version mismatch is the cause. ## Root Cause 1. `cmd_update` runs `check_config_version()` + `migrate_config()` for the **active** `HERMES_HOME` only — it never iterates over named profiles. 2. `cmd_dashboard` (which handles both `hermes serve` and `hermes dashboard`) does **not** run config version check/migration at startup, so a stale profile config goes unnoticed until agent init fails. ## Fix **1. `cmd_dashboard` — auto-migrate on startup** Add a non-interactive config version check + auto-migration before `start_server()`, mirroring the `version_bump_only` path the CLI already uses in `cmd_update`. If the config is stale but no new settings are needed, it silently migrates. If new required settings are needed, it prints a warning telling the user to run `hermes config migrate`. **2. `cmd_update` — migrate all profiles** After migrating the active profile, iterate over all named profiles via `list_profiles()` and migrate each one with the same non-interactive path. This ensures a single `hermes update` catches up every profile, not just the default. ## Behavior - **Version-bump-only** (no new settings): silently auto-migrated ✅ - **New required settings**: warning printed, user told to run `hermes config migrate` ⚠️ - **Migration failure**: swallowed (non-fatal) — `start_server` surfaces real config errors - **No profiles / no stale config**: no-op, zero overhead ✅ ## Testing - `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py` — 155/155 passed ✅ - `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py` — 151/151 passed ✅ - `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_config_clears_custom_fields.py` — 4/4 passed ✅ - `python -c "import hermes_cli.main"` — import OK ✅ Closes #20438 Closes #54926

signals.title: fix(cron): record no_agent runs as sessions so they show in run history
signals.text: ## Problem `no_agent: true` cron jobs (script-only watchdogs) create **zero feedback** when manually triggered from the Desktop GUI — no running indicator, no run record in Run History. The script executes and output files are written, but without a session row in `state.db` the GUI has nothing to display. ## Root Cause In `cron/scheduler.py`, the `no_agent` branch short-circuits before `SessionDB` is ever touched. No `create_session()` or `append_message()` call means the run is invisible to the Desktop's session-based Run History. ## Fix Create a `cron_{job_id}_{timestamp}` session row in the `no_agent` branch, mirroring what the agent path does: 1. `SessionDB.create_session(session_id, source="cron")` — creates the row 2. `SessionDB.append_message(session_id, "user", "no_agent script: {path}")` — seeds the preview 3. `SessionDB.append_message(session_id, "assistant", run_doc)` — records the output on completion This is the same pattern already used by the agent path. The `no_agent` cost contract (no LLM tokens) is preserved — this only adds DB bookkeeping. ## History This is the third submission of the same fix: - **#44087** (by AIalliAI, Jun 11) — closed by cleanup sweep (not technical rejection): *"If the fix is still needed, rebase and reopen."* - **#53692** (by me, Jun 27) — closed as duplicate of #44087 - **This PR** — rebased onto latest `origin/main`, all tests pass The fix has been confirmed effective by 3 independent users: AIalliAI, rebootcrab-blip, and yingliang-zhang. ## Test - 237 tests passed across `test_cron_no_agent.py` (114) and `test_scheduler.py` (123), 0 failed - Includes regression tests verifying session row creation and message persistence for `no_agent` runs
signals.author: yingliang-zhang

signals.title: fix(cron): reap stale sessions on every tick + persist final_response as session message
signals.text: ## Summary Two independent fixes for cron Run History issues (#46979): ### 1. Runtime stale-session reaper (every tick, not just startup) The startup-only `_cleanup_stale_cron_sessions()` catches sessions left open by a previous process lifecycle (SIGTERM/crash). But sessions can also get stuck in the *current* process when `run_job()`'s `end_session()` call is swallowed by a broad except clause — the broad excepts log at DEBUG and continue, leaving `ended_at IS NULL` forever. This makes Run History unreliable (sessions appear as permanently running) and prevents the report from being visible in the Desktop cron panel. **Fix:** - Add `SessionDB.close_stale_cron_sessions_by_age()` — closes cron sessions whose `started_at` exceeds a threshold, leaving legitimately running jobs untouched. - Add `_reap_stale_cron_sessions()` to `cron/scheduler.py` — called on every `tick()`, uses a 45-min threshold (well above the 600s child_timeout and typical 20-min max run time). - Includes the startup cleanup from #55386 to make this PR self-contained. ### 2. Persist final_response as assistant message in session DB The agent path in `run_job()` extracts `final_response` from the agent's last turn and uses it to build the output file (saved to disk) and for delivery. But it was never appended as an assistant message to the session DB. This meant that when a user opened a cron run session in Desktop's Run History, they saw the conversation (prompt, tool calls, intermediate reasoning) but NOT the final report — making it look like the cron run produced nothing. The no_agent path already has `_record_run()` which appends the output as an assistant message. The agent path had no equivalent. **Fix:** Append `final_response` as an assistant message right before returning from the success path, with the same broad-except pattern used by the surrounding `end_session`/`close` calls. ## Tests - `test_close_stale_cron_sessions_by_age_closes_old` — verifies only old cron sessions are closed, recent ones and non-cron sessions left alone - `test_close_stale_cron_sessions_by_age_idempotent` — second call is a no-op - All existing `test_hermes_state.py` tests pass (344 passed) ## Related - Fixes #46979 (Run History empty for agent cron jobs) - Supersedes #55386 (startup cleanup is included here for self-containment)
signals.author: yingliang-zhang

signals.title: fix(desktop): treat interrupted completions as metadata
signals.text: ## Summary - represent cancelled model waits as `interrupted` status with an empty final response instead of assistant prose - preserve real partial assistant text while keeping cancellation-only turns out of canonical session history - close interrupted `tool -> user` tails only in the per-request API copy so strict providers still receive valid ordering - settle Desktop interruption events without completion sounds, celebration/unread cues, or native completion notifications - keep narrow compatibility filtering for interruption sentinels emitted by older workers ## Root cause The core loop returned local cancellation status strings such as `Operation interrupted: waiting for model response (...)` as `final_response`, and the turn finalizer could persist a synthetic `Operation interrupted.` assistant row after a tool result. Desktop then handled every `message.complete` as a successful completion, so cancellation metadata appeared as a reply and triggered completion UX. The fix makes structured `interrupted` state authoritative. Empty cancellations stay metadata-only; actual streamed partial text is still returned and persisted. Provider role repair now happens on the API copy rather than rewriting the durable transcript. ## Verification - `pytest -q tests/run_agent/test_message_sequence_repair.py tests/agent/test_turn_finalizer*.py tests/agent/test_interrupt_tool_tail_api_sanitization.py tests/run_agent/test_run_agent.py -k 'interrupt or tool_tail or sanitize'` — 37 passed - `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream --environment jsdom` — 12 passed - `npm run typecheck` in `apps/desktop` — passed - focused Desktop ESLint — passed - `uv run --frozen --extra dev --extra acp pytest -q tests/acp/test_server.py -k interrupt` — 1 passed - `npx vitest run src/__tests__/createGatewayEventHandler.test.ts -t 'interrupt'` in `ui-tui` — 2 passed - focused Ruff and `git diff --check` — passed ## Related work This is complementary to #55317: that PR surfaces **non-interrupted** tool-result-only endings, while this PR keeps **interrupted** cancellation paths metadata-only.

signals.title: fix: preserve queued prompt boundaries end to end
signals.text: Fixes #45560. ## Summary - replace the busy-session single string slot with an ordered FIFO that keeps each submitted prompt, transport, timestamp, and stable source ID separate - persist each source prompt as its own user row so Desktop hydration can restore distinct bubbles - make explicit Desktop queue IDs idempotent across inflight, queued, history, and timeout/resume persistence states - preserve adjacent user messages as distinct canonical objects; merge only the transient provider copy for strict role alternation - add an explicit wire-only `[Next user message]` marker so the model still sees the semantic boundary - strip transcript-only timestamp/message-ID metadata at the common API-copy boundary and in Chat Completions transport defense-in-depth ## Root cause `tui_gateway._enqueue_prompt` stored one pending prompt. A second busy-time submission replaced that source boundary with `prev + "\n\n" + text`, so queueing, SessionDB, and Desktop hydration could never recover two independently submitted messages. A second destructive merge existed in `repair_message_sequence`: consecutive canonical user dicts were collapsed in place before API construction. That also changed the DB flush cursor and erased source identity even when the gateway had preserved it. This PR keeps source messages separate through the canonical queue/history/DB path. Provider-only role repair runs on copied API messages, where adjacent users are merged with an explicit boundary marker. No synthetic assistant bubble is added to canonical history. ## Exactly-once behavior Desktop reuses the queue entry ID when a timed-out submission resumes and retries. The gateway now acknowledges an explicit ID already present in the inflight turn, FIFO, canonical history, or SessionDB instead of interrupting/enqueuing it again. JSON-RPC request IDs are deliberately not used for deduplication because clients may reuse them after reconnect. ## Verification - Python focused matrix covering canonical/wire repair, FIFO integration, SessionDB persistence, idempotency, cursor repair, transport metadata, timestamps, and gateway group paths — **265 passed** - complete `tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py` with standalone-TUI environment — **316 passed** - final `tests/test_tui_gateway_queue_on_busy.py` — **16 passed** - Desktop composer queue + prompt actions Vitest — **57 passed** - Desktop `npm run typecheck` and focused ESLint — passed - focused Ruff and `git diff --check` — passed The six warnings in the 265-test run are existing `pkg_resources`/datetime deprecations from `lark_oapi` during Telegram configuration tests. ## Relation to #46459 #46459 preserves chronology by writing `[Later user message]` into text that is still canonically merged. This PR is an independent end-to-end fix for the uncovered `tui_gateway` single-slot/DB/Desktop path and uses a different architecture: canonical objects remain separate, while a separately implemented `[Next user message]` marker exists only in the provider wire copy. No code from #46459 is included.

signals.title: fix(tui): preserve foreground turns across background completion
signals.text: ## Problem When a background delegation completes while the user is viewing a busy session, the TUI gateway auto-fires a follow-up turn from the completion notification. Two UX bugs result: 1. **Surprise thinking after a forced report** — the user types `/report`, the assistant prints its findings and the turn ends; 77 ms later `drain_notifications` delivers the queued completion, and the model silently starts "thinking" again with no user prompt. The user has no idea why the agent re-engaged. 2. **Duplicate reply to the user's latest question** — the auto-resume runs to completion, then the user's actual pending prompt (queued during the internal turn) is drained and answered too — so the user sees two answers to what they asked once. The root cause is architectural: the gateway treats a background-process completion identically to a user-initiated prompt. It has no concept of *turn origin* — whether the current turn was started by the user, by a background notification, or by a `/goal` continuation — so it cannot tell the frontend to handle the three cases differently. ## Fix Introduce `TurnOrigin = Literal["user", "notification", "goal"]` and propagate it through every turn lifecycle boundary so the frontend can distinguish the three origins and apply origin-aware control flow. ### Backend (`tui_gateway/server.py`, `run_agent.py`) - **Turn origin + generation token.** `_run_prompt_submit` accepts `origin=` and stamps it into the session under a monotonic `turn_token`. Stale turns cannot clear state set by a newer turn. `message.start`, `message.complete`, and `session.info` all carry `turn_origin`. - **Deferred notifications.** When a user-origin turn hits `max_iterations_reached`, the gateway sets `defer_notifications_until_user = True` and queues any subsequent completion notifications into `deferred_notification_texts`. The next real user prompt claims the batch, prepends it as context to the user's message, and runs a single combined turn — no silent auto-resume, no duplicate reply. - **Deferred batch recovery.** If the user turn fails or is blocked (context-reference block), the claimed notifications are restored ahead of any concurrently arriving ones, so nothing is lost. - **Notification dispatch failure resilience.** `_drain_post_turn_notifications` and `_notification_poller_loop` catch synchronous dispatch exceptions, requeue the current and remaining events, log once, and continue — a single bad dispatch no longer terminates the poller or drops a drained batch. - **Clean persistence copy.** `_message_for_persistence` replaces the old in-place mutation: SQLite flush and JSON snapshot each get a non-mutating copy with clean user text, while the live API-facing message list (including multimodal image/audio parts) stays untouched. ### Desktop (`apps/desktop/src/`) - **Notification preemption.** When the user submits while a notification-origin turn is busy, the composer queues the draft and calls `cancelRun({ preserveBusyUntilSettled: true })` — the interrupt fires immediately, but `busy` stays true until the terminal `message.complete`/`session.info running:false` settles the turn. Only then is the queued draft drained and submitted exactly once. - **Feedback suppression.** An interrupted notification-origin completion suppresses completion sound, pet celebration, unread/mail state, and native OS notifications. The transcript and busy-state settlement still occur. - **Turn-origin state.** `ClientSessionState.turnOrigin` tracks the current origin via `session.info`, `message.start`, and `message.complete`. The status bar shows "Processing background result" for notification turns instead of generic thinking. ### Ink TUI (`ui-tui/src/`) - `TurnOrigin` type added to `types.ts`; `gatewayTypes.ts` extends `message.start`, `message.complete`, and `SessionInfo` with optional `turn_origin`. ### Tests | Layer | New/modified tests | |---|---| | Python gateway | `test_turn_origin_notifications.py` (12 tests): turn-origin token stale-clear, max-iteration deferral + clean-context claim, failed-turn batch restore, context-block batch restore, post-turn dispatch failure requeue, poller retry after dispatch failure | | Python agent | `test_860_dedup.py` (+1): multimodal persistence copy retains media marker without mutating live message; `test_run_agent.py` (+2): JSON snapshot applies clean text and preserves multimodal media | | Desktop | `use-composer-submit.test.tsx` (5 tests): notification preemption queues + interrupts, user/goal stays queue-only, drain-after-interrupt exactly-once, interrupt-failure releases gate; `turn-origin.test.tsx` (2 tests): origin reconciliation + feedback suppression; `status-origin.test.tsx` (1 test): status origin label | | Modified | `test_tui_gateway_server.py`, `test_tui_gateway_queue_on_busy.py`, `test_run_agent.py`, `use-session-actions/utils.test.ts` | ## Verification | Check | Result | |---|---| | Python impacted regression (6 files, 768 tests) | **768 passed, 0 failed** | | Desktop focused Vitest (8 files) | **76 passed, 0 failed** | | Desktop `npm run typecheck` | **PASS** | | Ink TUI `npm run typecheck` | **PASS** | | Changed Desktop ESLint | **PASS** | | Python `ruff check` + `py_compile` | **PASS** | | `git diff --check` | **PASS** | | Prettier (changed files) | **PASS** | ## Related - Complementary to #61719 (session-isolation for notification routing) — this PR adds turn-origin semantics; #61719 adds ownership routing. They touch different sections of `server.py`. - Independent of #63597 (interim assistant message boundaries) and #62598 (system-marker role persistence). - #61858 (gateway user-priority queue) addresses the gateway-layer equivalent of the same priority problem; this PR handles the TUI-gateway/desktop side. No existing issue or PR covers the turn-origin + deferred-notification + frontend-preemption combination.

signals.title: fix(hindsight): bind retain work to enqueue-time session identity
signals.text: ## Summary - freeze automatic Hindsight retain batches at enqueue time so later session switches cannot retarget their bank, document, tags, scopes, metadata, or payload - serialize retain writer lifecycle and session-state transitions so accepted work drains in FIFO order or is explicitly abandoned without advancing the watermark - retain actual async-future/client ownership through timeout, reconnect, shutdown, and atexit cleanup - give every initial call, reconnect retry, and later retry a fresh deep copy of a private canonical batch ## Root cause Automatic retain callbacks previously read mutable provider/session state when the writer eventually executed. A session switch, reconnect, timeout, or shutdown could therefore rebind accepted work to the wrong session/bank, start queued work after abandonment, close a client while an async operation still owned it, or allow a failed mutating client to taint retry payloads. ## Scope This PR is intentionally limited to **retain identity and lifecycle**. Prefetch request/session identity is a separate state machine and is not changed here. ## Verification - Hindsight provider + memory session-switch suites: **145 passed** - deterministic race/barrier tests cover authoritative lifecycle state, abandonment, sentinel accounting, reconnect ownership, async future lifetime, repeated shutdown/atexit, FIFO watermark behavior, and mutating-client retry isolation - Ruff, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check`: passed - latest-main rebase range-diff: patch identical - independent hard review: **ACCEPT**, no P0–P2 findings

signals.title: fix(hindsight): bind prefetch work to session identity
signals.text: ## Summary - bind Hindsight prefetch requests and cache publication to the request-time session identity - reject stale explicit-session admission atomically before it can mutate the active prefetch generation - separate logical worker capacity from unresolved async-future/client ownership - serialize local-embedded reconnect, client replacement, deferred close, and shutdown with exact client identity - reserve client ownership before scheduler submission and roll it back exactly once on construction or scheduling failure - replace provider-lifetime closed-client retention with client-local markers, identity-checked weak references, and a bounded defensive fallback ## Why Prefetch work may outlive a session switch or embedded-daemon reconnect. Without request-time identity and an ownership fence, stale work could publish into a newer session, worker timeouts could consume logical capacity indefinitely, or reconnect/shutdown could close a client after its coroutine was accepted but before ownership was recorded. ## Verification - focused lifecycle regressions: 3 passed - `tests/plugins/memory/test_hindsight_provider.py`: 133 passed - memory switch/boundary matrix: 16 passed - Ruff: passed - `py_compile`: passed - `git diff --check`: passed - deterministic scheduler/publication barrier, construction/scheduler rollback, 64 reconnect cleanup, weakref identity-reuse, and exact-once close probes - independent final hard review: ACCEPT, no P0-P2 findings - latest `origin/main`: no intervening changes to the two scoped files; merge-tree clean

signals.title: fix: block stale write_file overwrites
signals.text: ## Context `write_file` is a full-file replacement tool. If the model has an older copy of a file in conversation context, it can use that stale copy as its working base and overwrite manual or external edits made after the last read. ## Problem The existing staleness checks only attached warnings after the write had already landed. That meant the guard could tell the model the file was stale while still allowing the data-loss overwrite that the warning was meant to prevent. ## Solution This adds an explicit full-file baseline for `write_file`: existing host-visible files need a current non-partial `read_file` or prior successful same-task `write_file` before full replacement is allowed. Known-stale baselines now fail closed before disk mutation, and the refusal tells the model to re-read, merge, and retry. Targeted `patch` remains warning-only and does not bless a later full-file overwrite. Fixes #65604
